title: Late-Presenting Myocardial Infarction With Separate Anomalous Right-Sided Origins of the Left Anterior Descending and Circumflex Arteries: A Case Report.
authors: Wassim Beladel; Youssef Zeryouh; Mohamed El Minaoui
abstract: The clinical significance of an anomalous aortic origin of a coronary artery depends on the proximal course and ostial morphology, not on the ectopic origin alone, and coexisting acute myocardial infarction and multivessel atherosclerotic disease can make culprit assignment and revascularization difficult. A 79-year-old man was diagnosed with a late-presenting high-lateral ST elevation myocardial infarction while being treated for urinary sepsis. He had no ongoing chest pain. The electrocardiogram showed sinus rhythm with a premature atrial contraction (PAC), a negative T wave in aVL, and a flattened T wave in lead I, and cardiac troponin was 4850 ng/L. Transthoracic echocardiography showed regional wall-motion abnormalities and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 45% to 50%. Coronary angiography on day 3 demonstrated a left anterior descending artery arising from the right coronary ostial region with a severe proximal stenosis and a left circumflex artery arising separately from the right coronary sinus with a severe proximal stenosis. The right coronary artery had no significant stenosis. After clinical stabilization and heart team review, elective percutaneous coronary intervention of the proximal left circumflex artery was performed 34 days after diagnostic angiography. A 3.5 x 28 mm everolimus-eluting stent was implanted, and the procedural report documented no significant residual stenosis and final Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction grade 3 flow. Intervention on the anomalous left anterior descending artery was deferred pending coronary computed tomography angiography. This case separates the management of a severe atherosclerotic lesion from risk assessment of an anomalous coronary origin. Invasive angiography did not establish the proximal course of the left anterior descending artery, and an interarterial or intramural course cannot be inferred from its right-sided origin. Because no acute thrombus, pre-intervention flow grade, or definitive culprit lesion was documented, the circumflex artery should be described as the presumed infarct-related artery and the delayed procedure as staged revascularization. Further management of the left anterior descending artery requires cross-sectional anatomical imaging and individualized assessment of ischemia, viability, functional status, and procedural risk.

title: Planned percutaneous coronary intervention around transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a GRADE-assessed meta-analysis of randomized trials.
authors: Ibrahim Gowaily; Abdelrahman Awad; Ahmed A Ibrahim; Mohamed S Elgendy; Ali Bin Abdul Jabbar; Abdalhakim Shubietah; Muhammad Ghallab; Ahmed Elmogy; Mohamed Abuelazm; Ahmed Aboeata
abstract:
Severe aortic stenosis and coronary artery disease frequently coexist in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). We compared planned percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) around TAVI with an initially conservative or deferred PCI strategy.
We searched PubMed, Cochrane, Scopus, and Web of Science through 15 April 2026. Risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Exploratory reconstruction was a secondary analysis. The study protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO with the following ID: CRD420261397950.
Three randomized controlled trials including 1156 patients were identified. Planned PCI was not associated with significant differences in all-cause mortality (risk ratio = 0.90, 95% CI = 0.70-1.15), trial-defined major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; risk ratio = 0.91, 95% CI = 0.70-1.18; supportive and exploratory because composite components differed), cardiovascular death (risk ratio = 0.74, 95% CI = 0.51-1.08), or myocardial infarction (risk ratio = 0.86, 95% CI = 0.45-1.63). It was associated with fewer urgent (risk ratio = 0.33, 95% CI = 0.13-0.87) and any subsequent revascularizations (risk ratio = 0.25, 95% CI = 0.07-0.87), but more trial-reported major bleeding (risk ratio = 1.57, 95% CI = 1.07-2.32; definitions varied) and any bleeding (risk ratio = 1.77, 95% CI = 1.27-2.47).
Routine planned PCI around TAVI was not shown to reduce mortality or major ischemic outcomes. It was associated with fewer subsequent revascularizations and more trial-reported major bleeding and any bleeding, supporting selective, individualized decision-making.

title: When History Returns: Hybrid Management of Syphilitic Aortitis Causing Severe Aortic Arch Branch Stenosis and Cerebral Hypoperfusion.
authors: Julia Al Mousli; Anders Håkanson; Jonas Malmstedt; David Lindström
abstract:
Cardiovascular manifestations of tertiary syphilis are rare in the antibiotic era, but important to consider in atypical vascular findings. These manifestations typically appear several years after the primary infection and may lead to structural damage in the cardiovascular system, requiring surgical intervention despite appropriate antibiotic therapy.
This case describes a rare manifestation of cardiovascular syphilis in a 46 year old woman presenting with dizziness, pre-syncope, and syncope consistent with global cerebral ischaemia. Extensive evaluation revealed syphilitic aortitis with severe stenosis and or occlusion of all the major aortic arch branches. The patient was managed with antibiotic therapy in combination with surgical revascularisation. Both endovascular and open surgical approaches were used to restore blood flow to the left common carotid, left vertebral, and left subclavian arteries. This intervention improved cerebral perfusion and resolved the patient's symptoms. At two years, the carotid stent was patent, while the carotid subclavian bypass was occluded. The patient remained free from cerebral ischaemic symptoms but reported bilateral arm claudication.
Tertiary syphilis should be considered as a differential diagnosis when atypical arterial disease is encountered. Hybrid revascularisation may provide an effective, less invasive treatment strategy.

title: Impact of True and False Lumen Origins on Target Vessel Instability in Post-Dissection F/BEVAR.
authors: Vivian C Gomes; Mark A Farber; Adam W Beck; Matthew J Eagleton; Gustavo S Oderich; Lucas R Kanamori; Bruno Schmid; Andres Schanzer; Matthew P Sweet; Sara L Zettervall; Carlos H Timaran; Xingsheng Li; Ryan S Cantor; F Ezequiel Parodi; U.S. Aortic Research Consortium
abstract:
To evaluate the occurrence of target artery-related adverse events in post-dissection F/BEVAR patients, based upon artery origin from the true or false lumen.
This is a multicenter, prospective, cohort study evaluating post-dissection patients treated with F/BEVAR, in the US Aortic Research Consortium. The primary endpoint was 5-year target vessel instability (TVI). Secondary endpoints included 5-year primary patency, freedom from secondary interventions (SIs), and type Ic and IIIc endoleaks. The analysis was performed on a per-vessel basis.
A total of 1052 target arteries were analyzed, primarily including the celiac, superior mesenteric, and renal arteries, with individual hepatic and splenic arteries occasionally incorporated in the repair. Of the 277 patients included, 75% were men, and 19% were black, with a mean age of 66.8 ± 10.3 years. The mean aneurysm sac diameter was 66.0 ± 11.4 mm, with extent II thoracoabdominal aneurysms being the most prevalent (72.6%) among this cohort. Technical success was obtained in 96% of the cases. As primary outcome, the incidence of target vessel instability (TVI) was significantly lower (P<0.001) among the true-lumen vessels (16.4%) compared to false-lumen (29.9%) and dual-lumen arteries (43.8%). As for the secondary outcomes, the incidence of type Ic endoleak was significantly higher (P=0.001) in false-lumen vessels (9.6%) and dual-lumen vessels (8.6%) compared to true-lumen vessels (3.3%). There was no significant difference in the incidence of type IIIc endoleak (p=0.241) or target vessel occlusion (P=0.458). Target artery stenosis was significantly more common among arteries originating from the false lumen compared to true lumen (2.6% vs 0.4%, P=0.009). Fenestrations were associated with a higher incidence (30.5%) of TVI when compared to branches (5.9% P=0.005), however, this was observed only among dual-lumen vessels. Arteries incorporated by a fenestration and that had a dual-lumen origin, were associated with a higher occurrence of secondary interventions (23.7%) compared to true-lumen vessels (8.6%, P=0.010). The same was not observed among the arteries incorporated by a branch configuration. The time-to-event analysis demonstrated a significantly higher 5-year freedom from TVI in true-lumen vessels compared to false and dual-lumen ones (True lumen: 83.6%; False=70.1 %; Dual=56.2 %; Log-rank P=0.0002). Freedom from secondary interventions at 5 years was significantly higher in true-lumen vessels compared to dual-lumen ones (Log-rank P=0.0104), but not to false-lumen arteries (Log-rank P=0.0847). The 5-year primary patency did not differ significantly among groups (True lumen: 98.3%; False = 92.6%; Dual=93.9%; Log-rank P=0.1368). On Cox proportional hazards analysis, dual-lumen (95% CI 1.24-3.28, p=0.005) and false-lumen (95% CI 1.04 - 2.60, p=0.0325) target arteries were associated with an increased hazard of TVI, when compared to true lumen arteries, having 2.02 (P=0.005) and 1.65 (P=0.0325) times more risk of presenting TVI than a true-lumen vessel CONCLUSIONS: In F/BEVAR for post-dissection aneurysms, target vessel instability and secondary intervention are significantly lower in target arteries originating from the true lumen, when compared to false-lumen or dual-lumen vessels. Device design, with use of fenestrations or branches may also play a role, with a significant difference only observed in dual-lumen target arteries.

title: Post-mortem CT angiography for fatal vascular lesions in forensic death investigation: a systematic review of diagnostic performance, added value, and pitfalls.
authors: Luca Marinelli; Fiammetta Cappabianca; Salvatore Cappabianca
abstract:
Post-mortem CT angiography (PMCTA) is increasingly used in forensic death investigation to assess vascular disease, haemorrhage, and traumatic or natural vascular causes of death. However, its practical value depends on the lesion being investigated, the angiographic protocol, and the way imaging findings are integrated with autopsy and pathology. This systematic review evaluated the diagnostic performance, added value, and main pitfalls of PMCTA for fatal vascular lesions.
PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane/CENTRAL were searched for human post-mortem studies evaluating PMCTA in forensic, medico-legal, coronial, or post-mortem settings. Eligible studies compared PMCTA with autopsy, histopathology, targeted vascular dissection, or autopsy-based consensus. Evidence was grouped according to practical forensic use, including coronary stenosis assessment, autopsy triage, global vascular lesion detection, haemorrhage-source localization, aortic or traumatic vascular injury assessment, coronary plaque characterization, and artifact-related pitfalls. Risk of bias was assessed using a QUADAS-2-based approach adapted to forensic PMCTA studies.
The available evidence did not support unrestricted pooling of all fatal vascular lesions. PMCTA was used for different forensic questions, and only coronary stenosis provided data close to conventional diagnostic accuracy assessment. In this domain, available studies showed high specificity but only moderate sensitivity for critical stenosis. Autopsy-triage studies suggested that PMCTA may reduce or guide invasive autopsy in selected adult coronial workflows. Global comparison studies showed added value for vascular lesion detection, and haemorrhage-source studies suggested that PMCTA may help localize bleeding vessels. Evidence on fatal coronary plaque characterization is emerging. Pitfall studies showed that post-mortem clots, incomplete vascular filling, contrast leakage, and extravasation artifacts may mimic or obscure vascular pathology.
PMCTA is best interpreted as a complementary tool in forensic vascular death investigation rather than as a general substitute for autopsy. Its contribution is strongest when it answers a specific vascular question, such as documenting coronary stenosis, guiding autopsy, mapping vascular lesions, localizing haemorrhage, or supporting targeted histopathology. Careful correlation with autopsy, pathology, case circumstances, and protocol-related artifacts remains essential.

title: Impact of Right Heart Damage on the Prognostic Value of LV Mass Regression After TAVR.
authors: Hyun Jin Ahn; Jeehoon Kang; Minju Han; Seokhun Yang; Doyeon Hwang; Jung-Kyu Han; Han-Mo Yang; Kyung-Woo Park; Hyun-Jae Kang; Bon-Kwon Koo; Hyo-Soo Kim
abstract:
Left ventricular mass index (LVMI) regression after aortic valve replacement is associated with myocardial recovery and improved outcomes, but its prognostic relevance in advanced cardiac damage, particularly right heart involvement, is uncertain.
The authors aimed to determine whether the prognostic relevance of LVMI regression after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) differs according to right heart damage.
We retrospectively analyzed data from 548 patients with severe aortic stenosis who underwent TAVR between 2011 and 2023. Extravalvular cardiac damage was staged by echocardiography as stages 0 to 2 (no right heart damage) or stages 3 to 4 (right heart damage). LVMI regression was defined as a reduction from baseline to 1 month after TAVR. The primary composite endpoint was cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization.
Among the cohort (median age 81.0 [77.0-85.0] years; 51.3% women [281/548]), 9.1% (50/548) exhibited right heart damage. LVMI decreased after TAVR in both groups. Over a median follow-up of 1,020 (Q1-Q3: 552-1,731) days, LVMI regression was associated with lower risk of the primary endpoint in patients without right heart damage (adjusted HR: 0.59; 95% CI: 0.36-0.97; P = 0.04), whereas no association was observed in those with right heart damage (adjusted HR: 1.58; 95% CI: 0.40-6.27; P = 0.51) (P for interaction = 0.47).
Although LVMI regression occurred after TAVR regardless of right heart involvement, an association with improved clinical outcomes was observed in patients without right heart damage but not in those with right heart damage; however, given the nonsignificant interaction test, this finding should be considered hypothesis-generating.

title: Anatomically high-risk features, functionally benign: CT-FFR-guided assessment of coronary artery anomalies-case report.
authors: Şevval İlke Ebeoğlu; İpek Aydın; Abdullah Ömer Ebeoğlu; Ahmet Yıldız; Diaa Abdel Hakim; Emir Barış Özgür Ökçün
abstract:
Anomalous aortic origin of a coronary artery (AAOCA) can show anatomically high-risk features on coronary computed tomographic angiography (CCTA), yet ischaemia may be dynamic and not proportional to anatomic appearance. Computed tomographic-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) provides lesion-specific physiologic information from routine CCTA datasets and may aid management when anatomy and symptoms are discordant.
We describe three adults evaluated with CCTA and adjunct CT-FFR (DeepVessel FFR). Case 1: a 61-year-old asymptomatic man with anomalous right coronary artery (RCA) origin from the left coronary sinus and an interarterial course; CT-FFR 0.94-0.95 and normal myocardial perfusion scintigraphy supported conservative management. Case 2: a 23-year-old woman with intermittent, non-exertional chest discomfort and a family history of sudden cardiac death; CCTA showed a rare left main coronary artery origin from the non-coronary sinus with a retroaortic course; CT-FFR remained >0.80 (left anterior descending [LAD] 0.87; left circumflex [LCX] 0.88) and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) excluded left main coronary artery (LM) ostial stenosis (minimum lumen area [MLA] 11 mm2). Case 3: a 50-year-old asymptomatic man with an anomalous RCA from the left coronary sinus and an interarterial course; CT-FFR nadir was 0.87, and Heart Team discussion supported conservative management. Follow-up (6-12 months) was uneventful.
CT-FFR may complement anatomic assessment in selected adults with AAOCA and help avoid unnecessary invasive testing. However, because CT-FFR is derived from resting CCTA it cannot exclude exertion-dependent dynamic compression; persistent concern should prompt stress testing and/or invasive physiologic and intravascular assessment.

title: Ventricularis delamination causing acute left main obstruction during TAVI: a case report.
authors: Bo Fu; Fenlong Xue; Xiquan Song; Qingliang Chen; Nan Jiang
abstract:
Acute coronary obstruction is a rare but potentially fatal complication of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), most commonly resulting from displacement of a calcified native leaflet. We describe an unusual mechanism involving delamination of native aortic leaflet tissue with subsequent coronary ostial obstruction.
An 80-year-old woman with severe symptomatic calcific aortic stenosis underwent transfemoral TAVI with a self-expanding valve. During valve deployment, she developed abrupt haemodynamic collapse with marked ST-segment elevation. Emergency angiography demonstrated acute left main coronary obstruction, while transoesophageal echocardiography revealed a newly developed mobile flap-like structure in the ascending aorta, raising concern for acute aortic dissection. Emergency surgical exploration excluded aortic dissection and demonstrated delamination of native aortic leaflet tissue, macroscopically considered to involve the ventricularis layer. The detached tissue had prolapsed into the left coronary ostium, causing mechanical obstruction of coronary inflow. Excision of the obstructing tissue and surgical aortic valve replacement restored coronary perfusion.
This case expands the mechanistic spectrum of TAVI-related coronary obstruction and highlights an important diagnostic pitfall. Native leaflet delamination may produce a mobile intra-aortic flap mimicking acute aortic dissection while simultaneously causing catastrophic coronary obstruction. Recognition of this rare mechanism may facilitate prompt diagnosis and appropriate rescue intervention.

title: A Novel Intraluminal Microtube Anastomosis System (IMAS) for Rapid Rat Microvascular Reconstruction: Development and Experimental Evaluation.
authors: Sam-Youl Yoon
abstract: Background/Objectives: Conventional interrupted microvascular anastomosis is technically demanding and time-consuming. We developed an intraluminal microtube anastomosis system (IMAS) in which circumferential anchoring ridges on the outer surface mechanically retain each arterial end while two external circumferential ligatures secure the reconstruction. This study compared IMAS with conventional interrupted microsurgical anastomosis in a rat infrarenal abdominal aortic model. Methods: Forty male Sprague Dawley rats (250-300 g) were allocated to IMAS (n = 20) or conventional interrupted microsurgical anastomosis (n = 20). Random-sequence generation and allocation concealment were handled by an animal-experiment assistant. All formal procedures were performed by the same surgeon, who was proficient in conventional microsuturing and had completed 10 pilot IMAS procedures before the study. Anastomosis time was measured from complete aortic transection to restoration of flow after clamp removal. Patency was assessed at 1 week and 1 month by color Doppler ultrasonography, with terminal gross examination at 1 month. The study was exploratory and was not powered as a patency non-inferiority or equivalence study. Results: Mean anastomosis time was 5 min 30 s ± 60 s with IMAS and 20 min 32 s ± 75 s with conventional suturing (p < 0.001). The between-group mean difference (conventional minus IMAS) was 902 s (95% CI, 859-945 s), corresponding to an approximately 73% reduction. Patency was 19/20 (95%) in both groups at 1 week (p = 1.000) and 18/20 (90%) in both groups at 1 month (p = 1.000). No gross device migration, aneurysmal dilatation, or anastomotic leakage was observed in patent IMAS-treated vessels at necropsy. Conclusions: In this exploratory rat model, IMAS substantially shortened reconstruction time. The observed short-term patency proportions were the same in the two groups, but the study was not sufficiently powered to establish equivalence or non-inferiority in patency. Histological response, lumen stenosis, quantitative flow, mechanical strength, material biocompatibility, and longer-term outcomes require further evaluation.

title: The Fate of Mitral Valve Regurgitation After TAVI.
authors: Karin Steiner; Melchior Burri; Nina Feirer; Tobias Rheude; Hendrik Ruge; Markus Krane; Keti Vitanova
abstract: Background: Outcomes of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) for severe aortic stenosis with concomitant severe mitral regurgitation (MR) remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to quantify the evolution of high-grade MR after TAVI, compare changes using MR etiology, and assess associations between MR etiology, early improvement, or residual discharge MR and mortality. Methods: In a retrospective single-center cohort, 112 TAVI patients with baseline more-than-moderate MR were included (functional n = 94; degenerative n = 18). MR grade was assessed pre-TAVI, at discharge, and at last available follow-up (serial studies up to ≥5 years), and 5-year all-cause mortality was analyzed. Results: At discharge, 34% of patients improved by more than one MR grade, and 26% by one grade. Among 45 patients with available late echocardiographic follow-up, 62% improved by more than one grade, 24% by one grade. Exploratory five-year survival analyses did not demonstrate a significant difference for MR etiology (p = 0.23), discharge MR grade (p = 0.11), or MR improvement status (p = 0.12). Conclusions: Among patients surviving to longitudinal echocardiographic follow-up, MR reduction was frequently observed after TAVI. Exploratory analyses did not demonstrate statistically significant differences in 5-year survival according to MR etiology, early MR improvement, or discharge MR severity. However, limited sample size and incomplete follow-up preclude definitive prognostic conclusions. Overall, these findings are compatible with a surveillance-first management, and with individualized consideration of adjunctive mitral therapy for persistent higher-grade symptomatic MR.

title: Self-Expanding Stent-Assisted Reconstruction of Distal Supra-Aortic Vessels in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: A Comparative Analysis.
authors: Bowen Li; Feng Shi; Zhipeng Hu; Zongli Ren; Zhiyong Wu; Luocheng Li; Zhiwei Wang
abstract: Background: Supra-aortic vessel reconstruction during total aortic arch replacement in acute Stanford type A aortic dissection patients with dissected distal supra-aortic vessels remains technically challenging; proximal supra-aortic vessel replacement alone carries a high risk of neurological complications secondary to intimal inversion. This study aims to evaluate clinical outcomes of self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction compared with proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone. Methods and Results: We performed a single-center retrospective comparative analysis of 49 consecutive patients undergoing emergency total aortic arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection from January 2022 to December 2023. Patients were divided into two groups according to intraoperative anatomy and surgeon decision: self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction (SAVR, n = 26) and proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone (PRVA, n = 23). Neurological outcomes related to supra-aortic vessel intimal inversion, operative parameters, blood product transfusion, and short-term complications were analyzed. The mean follow-up was 18.2 ± 4.1 months (range, 12-24 months). The SAVR group exhibited significantly lower supra-aortic vessel stenosis rate (3.8% vs. 30.4%, p < 0.001) and zero cases of intimal inversion-related luminal collapse versus five cases in the PRVA group (0 vs. 5, p = 0.02). Numerically fewer cases of symptomatic stroke (0% vs. 8.7%, p = 0.09) and radiographic cerebral infarction (3.8% vs. 13.0%, p = 0.17) were observed in the SAVR group, though the differences did not achieve statistical significance. Red blood cell and fresh frozen plasma transfusion requirements, mechanical ventilation duration, and ICU stay length were significantly lower in the SAVR cohort. Cardiopulmonary bypass time and 30-day mortality were comparable between groups. Conclusions: Self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction represents a promising technical option during total arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection with distal supra-aortic dissection, associated with superior branch vessel patency and favorable numerical trends in neurological and recovery-related endpoints, with a comparable early-term safety profile. Potential benefits require further validation in larger cohorts.

title: Staged Management with Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in a Patient with ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis, and Recurrent Cardiogenic Shock: A Case Report.
authors: Zhongheng Li; Weili Teng; Ruining Li; Liyun He; Dan Li; Lincheng Yang; Mengsha Gao; Ling Xu; Yupeng Wang; Ming Cui; Lijie Sun
abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Cardiogenic shock after successful culprit-vessel revascularization may remain multifactorial when important structural heart disease coexists. Case Presentation: We report an 81-year-old man with extensive anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, low-gradient calcific aortic stenosis (AS) with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, and cardiogenic shock. Primary percutaneous coronary intervention of a completely occluded proximal left anterior descending artery was performed under intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support. Echocardiography showed an aortic valve area of 0.53 cm2, a mean transvalvular gradient of 25 mmHg, and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 32%. Although the findings raised concern for a classical low-flow, low-gradient AS phenotype, the low-flow state and true-severe AS could not be formally confirmed because stroke-volume index, dobutamine stress echocardiography, and standardized CT calcium scoring were unavailable. After IABP removal on day 6, profound recurrent shock with lactic acidosis and multiorgan hypoperfusion developed on day 10. IABP reinsertion was followed by improvement in systemic perfusion, whereas brief trial-off periods reproduced hemodynamic and symptomatic deterioration. TAVR was performed on day 24 after recovery of end-organ function, discontinuation of vasoactive drugs, partial platelet recovery, and completion of CT-based procedural planning. IABP was removed the next day, and the patient was discharged on day 30 with an ejection fraction of 42%. Conclusions: Recurrent shock after successful culprit-vessel reperfusion should prompt reassessment for persistent structural hemodynamic burdens. Temporary support may serve as a bridge to recovery and individualized procedural planning in selected patients, but the observed improvement after TAVR represents a temporal association in a multifactorial shock state and should not be interpreted as evidence for routine IABP use in infarct-related cardiogenic shock or a predetermined delay before valve intervention.

title: Short- and Mid-Term Effects of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement on Heart Rate Variability in Patients With Aortic Valve Stenosis.
authors: Emre Pacaci; Abdullah Yildirim; Mert Evlice; Guluzar Tras; Cuma Suleymanoglu; Muhammet Salih Ates; Mukremin Coskun; Emre Sezici; Mustafa Ozan Gursoy; Omer Sen; Omer Genc; Ibrahim Halil Kurt
abstract:
Heart rate variability (HRV) reflects autonomic nervous system balance and has emerged as a potential prognostic marker in cardiovascular diseases. However, the relationship between HRV and mortality following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) remains unclear.
This prospective cohort study included 230 patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis who underwent TAVR between June 2022 and June 2024. Twenty-four-hour Holter electrocardiography recordings were obtained one day before and at 3 months after the procedure to assess HRV using both time- and frequency-domain parameters.
Among the 230 patients enrolled, the 12-month all-cause mortality rate was 14.3%. Among frequency-domain parameters, the pre-TAVR low frequency/high frequency (LF/HF) ratio improved markedly from 2.20±1.45 to 1.54±0.85 (p<0.001). In the time domain, standard deviation of NN intervals (89-103 ms, p=0.027), standard deviation of the averages of NN intervals (68-83 ms, p=0.003), and percentage of successive RR intervals (10.0%-12.0%, p=0.036) all showed significant improvements, while root mean square of successive RR interval differences remained unchanged. The pre-TAVR LF/HF ratio was significantly lower in survivors and provided the best discrimination for 1-year mortality prediction (area under the curve 0.815; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.750-0.881). Calibration analysis confirmed excellent predictive accuracy (C-index, 0.81; Brier score, 0.104; pseudo-R2, 0.285). Patients with a pre-TAVR LF/HF ratio>1.34 had significantly lower mortality at follow-up (hazard ratio [HR] 0.103; 95% CI 0.042-0.250; log-rank p<0.001), and this association remained significant in landmark analysis beyond 3 months (HR 0.163; log-rank p<0.001).
HRV parameters provide meaningful prognostic information in patients undergoing TAVR. Among them, a reduced pre-TAVR LF/HF ratio is independently associated with increased 1-year mortality and may serve as a practical, non-invasive marker for risk stratification.

title: Association Between Revascularization Timing and Outcomes for Coronary Artery Disease in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
authors: Masashi Yamaguchi; Futoshi Yamanaka; Koki Shishido; Noriaki Moriyama; Tomoki Ochiai; Hirokazu Miyashita; Yoichi Sugiyama; Daisuke Sato; Eiji Koyama; Kunihiko Shimizu; Kazuki Tobita; Takashi Matsumoto; Shingo Mizuno; Yutaka Tanaka; Masato Murakami; Shigeru Saito
abstract:
Coronary artery disease (CAD) is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS), yet the optimal timing of coronary revascularization in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain.
We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients with severe AS and stable CAD, defined as fractional flow reserve ≤0.80, instantaneous wave-free ratio ≤ 0.89, or visual stenosis ≥90%, who underwent TAVI between October 2013 and July 2023. Patients were categorized into two groups: PCI-first and TAVI-first. The primary endpoint was 1-year incidence of major adverse cardiac events (MACE: all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and unplanned revascularization). The secondary endpoint was 3-year MACE stratified by PCI after TAVI among the TAVI-first group.
Of 1126 TAVI patients, 209 met criteria for concomitant CAD (PCI-first, n = 112; TAVI-first, n = 97). The TAVI-first group had lower frailty and fewer New York Heart Association functional class III/IV symptoms, whereas the PCI-first group had more blood transfusions. At 1 year, the crude incidence of MACE was higher in the PCI-first group, although this difference was not significant after propensity score adjustment (HR 1.62; 95% CI 0.60-5.2; p = 0.36). Among TAVI-first group, patients who underwent PCI after TAVI had a lower incidence of MACE (log-rank p = 0.007), but the 90-day landmark analysis showed no significant difference (0/24 vs. 5/62 events; log-rank p = 0.23).
In patients with severe AS and CAD, a PCI-first strategy was associated with a higher incidence of bleeding and transfusion without improvement in short-term outcomes. A TAVI-first strategy with selective PCI during follow-up may be a reasonable alternative, although the long-term benefit of post-TAVI PCI awaits confirmation in randomized trials.

title: Task Force 4: Clinical Considerations for the Care of Athletes with Genetic Cardiomyopathies.
authors: Sabiha Gati; Michael J Ackerman; Aaron L Baggish; Jonathan H Kim; Benjamin D Levine; Martin Maron; Matthew Martinez; Sharlene M Day
journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
abstract: The updated AHA/ACC Scientific Statement on Clinical Considerations for Competitive Sports Participation for Athletes with Cardiovascular Conditions presents the clinical considerations for athletes with genetic cardiomyopathies, including hypertrophic, dilated, arrhythmogenic, and left ventricular hypertrabeculation. This ACSM Official Pronouncement complements the 2020 ACC/AHA Scientific Statement by providing athlete-specific context, practical guidance for shared decision-making, and genotype-informed risk assessment for competitive sports participation, moving away from blanket sports disqualifications. Sports participation recommendations for each condition are tailored to risk levels, symptomatology, and genotype. Regular follow-ups and close surveillance are advised. This evolving approach underscores the importance of individualized care, ongoing research, and the integration of new data to better inform shared decision-making on the risks and benefits of competitive sports in athletes with cardiomyopathies.

title: Preoperative Dependent Functional Status Is Associated with Worse 30-Day Pulmonary Complications in Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement: An Insight from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program Database From 2005-2021.
authors: Renxi Li; Deyanira J Prastein
abstract:
While current cardiac surgery risk scores do not account for preoperative functional status, it has been linked to adverse outcomes in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, in surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR), preoperative functional status remains underexplored.
To examine the impact of preoperative functional status on 30-day SAVR outcomes to provide insights into clinical decision-making and postoperative care. Methods: Patients undergoing SAVR were identified from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database from 2005 to 2021. A 1:3 propensity-score matching was applied to patients with dependent (DFS) and independent (IFS) functional status. Thirty-day outcomes were assessed.
After propensity-score matching, DFS and IFS patients showed similar mortality (11.11% vs. 9.42%, P = 0.39) and major adverse cardiovascular events (9.91% vs. 9.11%, P = 0.66). Patients with DFS had higher risks of pulmonary complications (29.43% vs. 21.64%, P < 0.01) including pneumonia (13.21% vs. 9.21%, P = 0.04) and prolonged mechanical ventilation over 48 hours (25.83% vs. 15.42%, P < 0.01) but lower bleeding requiring transfusion (51.65% vs. 67.49%, P < 0.01). DFS patients were more likely to be discharged not to home (71.52% vs. 47.75%, P < 0.01) and had longer operation time (315.2 ± 130.5 vs. 293.5 ± 119.8 min, P < 0.01) and LOS (18.47 ± 14.30 vs. 15.07 ± 12.83 days, P < 0.01).
While SAVR is relatively safe in eligible DFS patients considering its mortality and cardiac outcomes, it is imperative to emphasize preoperative functional status assessments and closely monitor postoperative pulmonary complications.

title: Aortic valve calcification and one-year paravalvular leak after transcatheter aortic valve replacement: limited role of asymmetry.
authors: Pragati Basera; Roya Anahita Mousavi; Chisom Enwere; Minel Soroa; Edgar Argulian; Leila Alizadeh; Marcos Ferrandez-Escarabajal; Carlo Mannina; Lakshay Chopra; Samin K Sharma; Annapoorna S Kini; Stamatios Lerakis
abstract:
Paravalvular leak (PVL) is a significant complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Although total aortic valve calcification (AVC) burden and self-expandable valves are predictors of PVL, the impact of leaflet-specific AVC asymmetry remains uncertain. The authors evaluated the association between AVC asymmetry and mild or greater PVL at 1 year after TAVR and its interaction with valve type.
Patients undergoing TAVR between January 2022 and May 2025 with preprocedural noncontrast cardiac computed tomography and 1-year transthoracic echocardiography were included. Asymmetric AVC was defined as greater than 50% of total AVC on a single cusp.
Among 530 patients (mean age, 79 ± 8 years; 45.5% female), 130 (24.5%) had mild or greater PVL at 1 year. Total AVC was higher in women (1747 vs 1125 AU; P less than .001) and men (2612 vs 2063 AU; P less than .001) with mild or greater PVL, with greater calcification across all cusps. AVC asymmetry was comparable between PVL and non-PVL groups (33.1% vs 41.4%; P = .093). Total AVC independently predicted PVL (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.036 per 100 AU; P < .001), whereas asymmetry did not (adjusted OR, 0.912; P = .681). No significant interaction occurred between valve type, AVC asymmetry, and PVL (P = .224).
Total AVC independently predicts mild or greater PVL at 1 year after TAVR, whereas leaflet-specific asymmetry and valve type provide no additional predictive value.

title: A rapid detection model and device for pH value in water quality based on ratio fluorescence imaging.
authors: Min Pu; Tingting Zhang; Guangqi Liu; Tai Ma; Minshou Wang; Ming Sun
journal: Water science and technology : a journal of the International Association on Water Pollution Research
abstract: pH value is a critical physicochemical parameter in water quality assessment. Deviations from the optimal pH range in aquatic environments such as rivers, lakes, and oceans can exert profound and lasting adverse effects on ecosystem stability and human health. In this study, a pH detection system integrating a ratiometric fluorescence imaging strategy was developed. A ratiometric fluorescent probe based on graphene quantum dots and gold nanoclusters was first constructed. Fluorescence imaging data were subsequently captured using a smartphone camera, followed by data augmentation and expansion to establish a robust ratiometric fluorescence image dataset. A hybrid pH detection algorithm combining YOLOv5n-based object detection and CatBoost regression was proposed and implemented. Furthermore, a portable device for on-site water pH measurement was assembled. The proposed model achieved a detection accuracy of 99.26%, demonstrating excellent performance. The practical applicability of the device was validated through pH measurements of real water samples, with comparative analyses against conventional methods confirming its superior detection capability. Overall, the developed pH sensor offers distinct advantages in terms of portability and cost-effectiveness, rendering it suitable for rapid, on-site pH monitoring in diverse water bodies.

title: Opportunistic Risk Assessment of Major Osteoporotic Fractures from Routine Chest Radiographs Using Deep Learning.
authors: Yisak Kim; Chang Min Park; Hanbin Ko; Dongheon Lee; Jin Hwan Kim; Sung Hye Kong
abstract:
Bone mineral density (BMD) and the Fracture Risk Assessment Tool (FRAX) incompletely capture fracture risk in the osteopenic range, where much of the fracture burden occurs. Routine chest radiographs are acquired across a broad range of patients and may contain information relevant to fracture risk, offering a potential opportunistic complement without additional imaging burden.
We developed a convolutional neural network survival model in 53,109 adults at a tertiary hospital and externally validated it in 85,284 patients from two independent institutions. Eligibility required a chest radiograph obtained within 1 year of dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry scans, so all participants had been referred for densitometry. The primary outcome was incident major osteoporotic fracture. Discrimination was assessed by using the concordance index (C-index) and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) at 2, 3, 5, and 10 years, compared with FRAX with BMD and with the lowest BMD T-score.
In the external validation cohorts (mean 58.6 years of age; 68.9% female; and follow-up of 77 months), the deep-learning (DL) model achieved a C-index of 0.843 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.837 to 0.850) and a censoring-adjusted 10-year AUROC of 0.855 (95% CI, 0.846 to 0.863), which was higher than that of FRAX with BMD (C-index, 0.779, 95% CI, 0.770 to 0.787; 10-year AUROC, 0.785, 95% CI, 0.775 to 0.794; both P<0.01). Adding FRAX to the DL model did not meaningfully improve discrimination (C-index, 0.847, 95% CI, 0.841 to 0.853). In the osteopenia subgroup (n=35,358), the DL model achieved a 10-year AUROC of 0.779 (95% CI, 0.764 to 0.795) versus 0.659 (95% CI, 0.641 to 0.676) for FRAX with BMD (P<0.01). This advantage was consistent across fracture types and BMD categories.
A survival DL model applied to routine chest radiographs identified patients at high fracture risk with discrimination exceeding that of FRAX, with the greatest benefit in patients with osteopenia. As all participants had been referred for densitometry, absolute-risk and case-finding estimates require prospective evaluation in an unselected routine-radiography population. (Funded by the National Research Foundation of Korea and others.).

title: Graph-based learning of nanopore translocation event signals.
authors: Mayukh Kansari; Tobias Ensslen; Jan C Behrends; Maria Fyta
abstract: Nanopores enable single-molecule analysis by measuring current signals through nanoscale pores in either biological or solid-state membranes. Accurate detection of analyte fingerprints within the pore environment is essential for reading-out the analyte type and sequence. Towards these aims, we develop a framework for robust, semi-supervised detection of molecular nanopore events on the basis of a graph representation of the measured signals. To this end, using experimental signals from DNA translocation through an aerolysin pore, we build a graph-based two-stage workflow employing convolutional and graph neural networks that first perform fast screening followed by deep validation of these nanopore events. The learned model is able to select possible molecular signatures (the current blockades) in the full signal, denoise, validate, and reconstruct them, and predict the morphology of unseen molecular events within the range of the available data. The trained model can efficiently predict the correct event morphology for the same analyte within a 2.4-fold range of transmembrane voltage values not included in the training. The developed partially supervised workflow, linking unsupervised graph representation-learning to raw-signal inference is - at its current state - a computational proof of concept that proposes a direction for the development of modular and generalizable event detection workflows, provided that they are trained on a huge amount of different nanopore experiments.

title: Predicting Cirrhotic Patients' Transition From Compensated to Decompensated Stage: A Graph-Based Multitask Deep Learning Method.
authors: Mohammadsadegh Abolhasani; Da Xu; Paul Jen-Hwa Hu; Ting-Shuo Huang
abstract:
Cirrhosis is a chronic liver disease, manifested by fibrosis and regenerative nodules. It can be classified clinically as compensated or decompensated. Accurate predictions of patients' transition from compensated to decompensated cirrhosis are important but difficult because of the multifactorial nature of disease progression, comorbid conditions, and patient heterogeneity.
To effectively identify at-risk patients with cirrhosis and facilitate timely interventions across chronic diseases and patient populations, this study aimed to develop a deep learning-based method to estimate patient transition from compensated to decompensated cirrhosis. The proposed method seeks to provide superior predictive utilities and help physicians derive actionable clinical insights by modeling comorbidity relationships and symptom interdependencies that influence the progression of cirrhosis among patients.
The proposed method was guided by clinical knowledge, considers patient demographics and medications, and leverages a graph structure to capture important comorbidity interplays. This method was augmented with post hoc interpretability to help clinicians understand its predictions for clinical decision-making and patient management. Using clinical data from 29,915 patients with cirrhosis, we evaluated the proposed method in comparison with 12 prevalent methods.
The proposed method attained an average area under the curve (AUC) of 0.871 (SD 0.004), F-measure of 0.678 (SD 0.010), recall of 0.741 (SD 0.022), and precision of 0.663 (SD 0.005). It showed a 6.09% improvement in AUC and a 13.95% improvement in F-measure over the best-performing benchmark method. Supported by post hoc interpretation analyses, this method can provide physicians with interpretable visualizations of the underlying comorbidity and symptom dynamics to better support their decision-making and adoption.
Empirical results underscore the value of demographic similarity, comorbidity graphs, and extended loss functions for identifying patients at higher risk of decompensation by capturing finer-grained information from essential patient features that tend to be overlooked by most existing methods. The proposed method not only supports physicians' clinical decision-making and patient management but can also enhance health care organizations' resource allocation efficiency and cost containment.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Standardizing Clinical Data Using Health Level Seven Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources: Development and Evaluation Study.
authors: Álvaro Riquelme-Tornel; Pedro Luis Costa Del Amo; Catalina Martínez-Costa
abstract:
One of the barriers to the wider adoption of clinical information modeling standards is the high cost associated with the time and effort required to model and map data from legacy systems, as well as the need for specialized modeling experts. Meanwhile, large language models (LLMs) are becoming powerful tools for data transformation and semantic processing.
The aim of this study was to evaluate the capability of LLMs to support the mapping of structured clinical data to Health Level Seven (HL7) Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) resources and attributes.
Using data from the MIMIC-IV (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV) database, a data pipeline integrating clustering techniques, retrieval-augmented resource grounding, and schema-guided prompting was implemented to support the FHIR mapping of structured clinical data. The pipeline was evaluated under 2 scenarios with different levels of complexity. In the first scenario, used as a baseline, the input data were well described and contextually rich. In the second scenario, designed as a controlled test under substantially reduced context, the original table structure and table-level descriptions were removed, while data element names and LLM-enriched descriptions were retained.
Using 65 data elements, top 2 resource identification accuracy reached 100% in the baseline scenario. The highest mean attribute-level mapping accuracy was 80.61% (SD 2.06) for GPT-4o and 69.54% (SD 5.15) for Llama 3.3 70B. In the low-context scenario, clustering-based context recovery increased top 5 resource identification accuracy to 94%. Across temperature settings, GPT-4o achieved mean attribute-level mapping accuracies ranging from 73.23% (SD 2.92) to 76.77% (SD 1.14), whereas Llama 3.3 70B ranged from 54.31% (SD 4.17) to 58.31% (SD 2.23). Error analysis showed that the main remaining failures were associated with resource-level confusion and terminal-attribute semantic ambiguity, whereas other error categories were comparatively infrequent.
LLMs can support structured clinical data mapping to HL7 FHIR, but fine-grained semantic disambiguation remains the principal limitation. In context-rich settings, the main errors occurred when selecting the appropriate terminal FHIR attribute. Under reduced context, accurate candidate-resource retrieval became increasingly important, and clustering-based context recovery substantially improved resource identification. These findings support the use of LLMs as assistive components within human-supervised interoperability workflows, with particular attention to candidate-resource selection and ambiguity-sensitive attribute mappings.

title: Letter to the Editor: Deep Learning-Based Detection of Sessile Serrated Lesions in Colonoscopy Images.

title: Deep Learning-Based Classification of Pulmonary Hypertension Using Early-Fused CTPA and Pulmonary Artery Segmentation Maps.
authors: Shoubo Hu; Mengyuan Li; Mu Li; Chi Zhang; Sheng Xie; Yue Lin; Deyu Li; Jin She
abstract: Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is vital for diagnosing pulmonary hypertension (PH), especially thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH). However, manual image interpretation of CTPA often leads to misdiagnosis. This study aims to automatically segment the pulmonary artery from CTPA images and develop a deep learning model by fusing CTPA images with pulmonary artery segmentation results to distinguish pulmonary hypertension (PH vs. subjects without PH (no-PH)) and its PH subtype, CTEPH (CTEPH, other PH vs. no-PH). The study included 92 patients with CTEPH, 85 patients with other types of PH, and 140 no-PH. We completed the image preprocessing and segmentation of the pulmonary arterial tree of all the sample data. Based on four deep learning model classifiers-ResNet50, DenseNet, SENet, and Swin Transformer, we respectively developed four distinct network architectures: Single input channel for CTPA images, as well as early, middle, and late fusion strategies that combine CTPA images with their corresponding pulmonary vascular segmentation maps. The performance of the testing experiments has shown that the DenseNet (CTPA-seg) early fusion model achieves optimal performance in the binary classification task of pulmonary hypertension (PH vs. no-PH), with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.927. Meanwhile, the Swin Transformer (CTPA-seg) early fusion model shows the best performance in the ternary classification of pulmonary hypertension subtypes (CTEPH, other PH vs. no-PH), achieving an AUC of 0.855. Compared with models that only use clinical images, the early feature fusion strategy shows significantly higher accuracy in classifying and diagnosing PH, which is beneficial for the differential diagnosis of CTEPH.

title: Molecular basis of reproductive plasticity in termites under environmental stresses and prediction of colony fecundity using machine learning.
authors: Chen-Xu Ye; Wen-Xiu Zhang; Xin-Yi Liu; Tian-Ge Zhang; Yuan-Yan Tian; Yan-Li Yang; Noor-Us Saba; Lian-Xi Xing; Sheng Li; Xiao-Hong Su
abstract: The reproductive plasticity of social insects provides colonies with tremendous flexibility to respond to environmental changes and adapt to new habitats. However, understanding how gene networks regulate this plasticity to generate complex social phenotypes remains a challenge. Here, we propose an "inhibition-activation-reinhibition" model for the reproductive transformation of female workers using three species of Reticulitermes termites. Through transcriptomic analysis of female workers during this dynamic cycle, we identified functional genes involved in their reproductive transformation. We found that gene expression profiles in female workers responded strongly to queen loss. Furthermore, we confirmed that under severe environmental stress that threatened colony survival, the workers did not activate the gene regulatory networks associated with reproductive transformation. We also demonstrated that piggyBac and tigger transposable element-derived genes in the workers' brains cooperatively promoted reproductive transformation. Metabolomic changes in female workers were linked to stress signals from queens and the nest environment, primarily involving fatty acid and amino acid metabolism pathways. Finally, we constructed seven machine learning models to elucidate gene expression profiles related to reproductive plasticity and to predict the presence and loss of female reproductives (queens, which are indicators of colony fecundity). Among these, the deep neural network models showed the highest accuracy and practicability for analyzing gene regulatory networks and predicting caste. We propose that female workers, as indicators, carry extensive colony-specific information at the transcriptomic level. These findings provide valuable insights and innovative methodologies for understanding reproductive plasticity in social insects under environmental stress.

title: CrystaL Artificial Intelligence Monitoring (CLAIM) Study of the OMERACT Ultrasound CPPD Subtask Working Group: Interim Analysis of Automated Ultrasound Grading of Knee Meniscal CPPD.
authors: Marco D Dal Fabbro; Tito Bassani; Daniele Cirillo; Rodolfo Fabbri; Alessandro Lucia; Laura Pezzoni; Luca Ingrao; Antonella Adinolfi; Edoardo Cipolletta; Luis Coronel; Mario Diaz; Andrea Di Matteo; Emilio Filippucci; Hilde Berner Hammer; Daryl MacCarter; Ingrid Möller; Mohammed A Mortada; Esperanza Naredo; Sara Nysom Christiansen; Greta Pellegrino; Francesco Porta; Garifallia Sakellariou; Wolfgang A Schmidt; Silvia Sirotti; Ouidade Aitisha Tabesh; Giorgio Tamborrini; Plamen Todorov; Otto Olivas-Vergara; Richard J Wakefield; Salvatore Gitto; Luca M Sconfienza; Carlos Pineda; Peter Mandl; Maria Antonietta D'Agostino; Lene Terslev; Georgios Filippou
abstract:
We aimed to develop and evaluate artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods for automated grading of calcium pyrophosphate deposition (CPPD) in ultrasound (US) images according to the Outcome Measures in Rheumatology (OMERACT) US scoring system.
Within the OMERACT CrystaL Artificial Intelligence Monitoring (CLAIM) project, two deep learning strategies were explored using knee meniscus US images graded from 0 to 3. Image-level classification was evaluated using convolutional neural networks (CNN) trained directly on cropped meniscus images (n = 446). A semantic segmentation approach was developed using a subset of 279 images with manually annotated masks identifying meniscus and deposits. Models were evaluated using an 80/20 training-validation split and stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Segmentation was assessed using Intersection over Union (IoU). For automated grading, an area ratio (AR), representing CPPD pixels relative to meniscus and CPPD pixels, was applied to predicted masks.
Image-level classification achieved an accuracy of 0.69 in the single-split analysis and a mean accuracy of 0.59 (SD 0.10) in 5-fold cross-validation. End-to-end AR grading achieved accuracies of 0.64 and 0.61 (SD 0.10), with a grade 3 recall of 0.25 in the single split. AR grading on manually annotated reference masks achieved an accuracy of 0.82. The best-performing segmentation model achieved mean IoUs of 0.86 for background, 0.60 for meniscus, and 0.37 for CPPD.
These findings provide a methodological basis for automated CPPD US grading, but performance remains far from clinical applicability, highlighting the need for larger datasets and improved segmentation.

title: Unified Deep Learning Framework for Interpretable Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Lithium-Ion Batteries under Stochastic Group-Behavioral Usage Scenarios.
authors: Yong Jin Jeong; Hyunjae Kim; Sangwon Jung; Seongha An; Yeonwoo Chae; Gahyun Lee; Inwoo Kim; Jun Hee Lee; Chun Yong Kang; Jang Wook Choi; Taesup Moon
abstract: With the widespread use of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) across various industries, accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is essential for end-users. However, stochastic degradation patterns under unpredictable real-world operations pose a fundamental challenge to conventional prognostic models. This study develops a unified deep learning-based framework for RUL prediction under group-behavioral usage scenarios. A group-behavioral battery dataset is constructed using synthesized charging protocols characterized by a unique Markov transition matrix designed to capture distinct group usage patterns. Systematic feature engineering identifies 13 health indicators (HIs) with strong predictive relevance to RUL. By utilizing these HIs across multiple learning models, the framework offers a flexible paradigm where lightweight models provide high-fidelity predictions or integrate into a weighted ensemble scheme to enhance accuracy and robustness. Across three heterogeneous datasets with varying cell chemistries and group behavioral patterns, the framework consistently yielded normalized root mean square errors (NRMSEs) ≤ 6.20%. Benchmarking against state-of-the-art (SOTA) architectures showed that systematic feature selection paired with lightweight learning models remained highly competitive with the tested complex architectures. By elucidating the underlying mechanisms of the HIs, the proposed framework enables interpretable and specialized RUL prediction tailored to group-specific driving patterns, highlighting its potential for real-world applications.

title: Transformer models in genomics: from sequence analysis to population genetics and biodiversity.
authors: Iqra Farooq; Sara Atito; Inga Prokopenko; Muhammad Awais; Ayse Demirkan
abstract: Modern genomics and artificial intelligence converge at a breakthrough point with the emergence of transformer-based large language models for genomic analysis. This review examines how transformer-based models have advanced genomic sequence analysis through novel tokenization strategies, self-attention mechanisms, and pre-training/fine-tuning paradigms. Unlike prior broad surveys, we focus on three sub-areas of genomics where transformer architectures have had a substantive impact: sequence-level analysis, population-level genetics, including genetic imputation and genome-wide association analysis, and biodiversity research, while addressing challenges like genome-scale computational demands, training biases, and interpreting attention in biological contexts. Looking forward, we outline how emerging foundation models, multi-modal integration, and biologically informed attention mechanisms could transform our understanding of genome function, providing a roadmap for leveraging genome language models to decode genome complexity and advance functional and population-level genomics.

title: [Influence of Deep Learning Reconstruction on the Detection of Susceptibility Effect by T2*-weighted Imaging].
authors: Takuma Daimaruya; Kazuhiko Oyu; Yohei Funato; Ryutaro Mori; Shingo Kakeda
abstract:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate the influence of DLR on the detection of susceptibility effects by T2*WI.
The imaging sequence was T2*WI using a 3.0 T MRI system. The phantom, assuming white matter, was made of diluted gadolinium contrast agent solidified with agar, and the susceptibility effect of bubbles in the phantom was evaluated. The slice thickness was varied from 1 to 5 mm, and images with and without DLR were acquired. The imaging was performed under conditions in which the number of averages was changed to adjust the SNR at each slice thickness, and also at 1 NEX separately. Binarization was performed on all slices, and the number of detections of the susceptibility effect was compared.
The number of detections of the susceptibility effect increased with DLR for slice thicknesses of 2-5 mm and did not differ by DLR for slice thicknesses of 1 mm. Under 1 NEX with DLR, the number of detections increased for slice thicknesses of 3-5 mm and decreased for slice thicknesses of 1 mm.
The results suggest that the number of detections of the susceptibility effect is higher when DLR is used. However, the behavior may vary depending on the SNR of the conventional image, so the image should be taken under guaranteed SNR conditions.

title: A decentralized federated learning approach for predicting chemoradiotherapy response from multicenter whole-slide images.
authors: Yuan Liu; Yuteng Pan; Yukun Tian; Shupeng Zhang; Qingdong Liu; Jianfeng Qiu; Hao Wang
abstract:
Given the institutional and regulatory barriers to centralized sharing of multicenter whole-slide image (WSI) data for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model development without requiring centralized sharing raw WSI data. This study explores a WSI-based FL model for predicting chemoradiotherapy response in advanced NSCLC, and compares its performance with centralized deep learning (DL) and clinical models using external multi-center validation cohorts.
This study collected WSI and corresponding clinical data from 250 patients across four hospitals. We developed a centralized DL model and a FL model based on WSI, with patch-level predictions aggregated to patient-level outcomes using a voting method. In addition, we built a clinical logistic regression model using clinical data. All models were evaluated on two independent external cohorts (Hospital C and Hospital D). Performance was summarized as the mean and 95% confidence interval across the five models obtained from five-fold cross-validation.
Across both external validation cohorts, WSI-based models consistently outperformed the clinical model. The FL model achieved performance comparable to the DL model. In hospital C, the DL model had an accuracy/AUC of 0.68/0.64, while the FL model achieved 0.70/0.65. The clinical model had an accuracy/AUC of 0.58/0.58. In hospital D, the DL model had an accuracy/AUC of 0.68/0.68, while the FL model achieved 0.73/0.71. The clinical model had an accuracy/AUC of 0.61/0.59.
The FL model using WSI achieved performance comparable to the centralized DL model in predicting NSCLC outcomes, while allowing each participating institution to retain its local data. It also showed consistent performance across independent external validation cohorts. This approach provides a practical solution for collaborative model development in multi-center pathology studies, particularly in settings where data sharing is restricted.

title: Performance of large language models in early orthodontic treatment: a comparative study of ChatGPT-5.4 and deepSeek-V3.2.
authors: Jialin Xu; Masahiro Nakamura; Rui Chen; Janvier Habumugisha; Gohji Kozaki; Ju Zhou; Takashi Izawa; Hiroshi Kamioka
abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used by patients and dental professionals to obtain orthodontic information. However, few studies have specifically compared the performance of LLMs in answering questions related to early orthodontic treatment, an area that requires complex clinical reasoning and high-quality patient education. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical applicability of ChatGPT-5.4 and DeepSeek-V3.2 in early orthodontic treatment using a multidimensional evaluation framework.
Five orthodontists developed 20 questions across five domains (age of treatment, adverse oral habits, early treatment, complications, and retention and relapse). The standard answers were derived from clinical guidelines, authoritative textbooks, and articles published in Q1 journal. Each question was submitted once to each LLMs. Responses were anonymised and independently evaluated by five blinded orthodontists. Accuracy and comprehensiveness were assessed using a five-point Likert-type framework combined with visual analogue scale (VAS)-based continuous scoring. Readability was calculated using the SMOG formula. References were cross-checked against five databases and were considered authentic when their bibliographic details corresponded to an indexed publication in at least one database. Thinking time, generation time, and word count were recorded. Inter-rater agreement was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Depending on the distribution of paired differences, paired t-tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were applied.
ChatGPT-5.4 showed significantly higher accuracy (9.03 ± 0.34 vs. 7.87 ± 0.95, p < 0.001) and comprehensiveness (4.49 ± 0.19 vs. 3.87 ± 0.54, p < 0.001) than DeepSeek-V3.2. DeepSeek-V3.2 was significantly faster (thinking time: 7.0 vs. 82.9 s; generation time: 39.4 vs. 133.4 s, both p < 0.001) and more readable (SMOG grade: 13.48 vs. 14.78, p = 0.003). No significant differences were observed for word count (p = 0.306) and reference authenticity (p = 0.895). In the domain analysis, ChatGPT-5.4 significantly outperformed DeepSeek-V3.2 in the domains of early treatment and retention and relapse (p < 0.05), whereas no significant differences were observed in the age of orthodontic treatment, adverse oral habits, and complications domains. Inter-rater agreement was good (ICC = 0.767-0.801).
ChatGPT-5.4 demonstrated greater accuracy and comprehensiveness, whereas DeepSeek-V3.2 generated responses more rapidly and produced more readable text. However, neither model achieved a readability level appropriate for the average patient. Neither model should replace professional clinical judgment.

title: Decomposing multi-scale dynamic regulation from single-cell multiomics with scMagnify.
authors: Xufeng Chen; Xi Yan; Bihan Shen; Heqi Wang; Zhixuan Tang; Yan Zang; Ping Lin; Haibing Zhang; Yu Li; Hong Li
abstract: Deciphering the highly coupled regulatory circuits that drive cellular dynamics remains a fundamental goal in biology. However, capturing the multi-scale time-lagged dynamics and combinatorial regulatory logic of gene regulation remains challenging. Here we present scMagnify, a deep-learning-based framework that leverages chromatin accessibility and gene expression via Granger causality to reconstruct and decompose multi-scale gene regulatory networks (GRNs). Diverse benchmarks demonstrate scMagnify's favorable performance. scMagnify employs tensor decomposition to identify combinatorial TF modules and their activation profiles across multiple time-lags. We applied scMagnify to human hematopoiesis and mouse pancreas development, where it recovered known lineage-driving regulators and provided further insights into the combinatorial logic underlying cell fate decisions. Furthermore, in the context of kidney injury, scMagnify's intercellular communication module mapped key signaling-to-transcription cascades linking microenvironment cues to pathological epithelial cell changes. In summary, scMagnify provides a robust computational framework for dissecting the multi-scale regulatory logic that governs complex biological processes in development and disease.

title: Advance care planning and care coordination for people with parkinsonism: a randomized controlled trial.
authors: Bauke W Dijkstra; Catharina Muente; Michela Garon; Kristina Rosqvist; Monica Scharfenort; Katharina M Lex; Laura E Grover; Eirini Nixina; Pille Taba; Ülle Krikmann; Katrin Sikk; Anette E Schrag; Philip Poku; Spyridon Konitsiotis; Miltiadis Makrydimas; Stefan Lorenzl; Per Odin; David J Pedrosa; Kris C P Vissers; Marieke M Groot; Bastiaan R Bloem; Marjan J Meinders; Angelo Antonini; PD_Pal consortium
abstract: Parkinsonism comprises a group of progressive neurodegenerative disorders, including Parkinson's disease and atypical parkinsonism. In advanced stages, advance care planning (ACP) and coordinated care are important to align treatment with patients' values and reduce unwanted interventions and caregiver burden. In this study we evaluated whether a nurse-led intervention increases documentation of end-of-life preferences and improves patient and caregiver outcomes. In this multicentre, single-blind randomized controlled trial (2020-2022), participants with parkinsonism (Hoehn & Yahr stage ≥3) and their caregivers were included across seven neurology centres in Austria, Estonia, Germany, Greece, Italy, Sweden, and the UK. Participants were randomized 1:1 to either the PD_Pal intervention (a structured six-month nurse-led ACP and care coordination program) or usual care. The primary outcome was documentation of end-of-life preferences at six months. A total of 189 people with parkinsonism and 189 family caregivers were enrolled. No significant difference was found in documentation of end-of-life preferences between groups (P = 0.77). Caregivers in the intervention group reported improved quality of life at six months (P = 0.03), although this effect was not sustained at 12 months. No differences were observed in other outcomes. These findings highlight challenges in implementing ACP in advanced parkinsonism and the need for flexible, stage-appropriate strategies.

title: Automated assessment of pediatric adenoid hypertrophy on lateral cephalograms using a deep learning-based keypoint approach.
authors: Jiale Han; Siyang Liu; Xiong Shi; Tianfan Cheng; Ruiqi Ni; Yongming Li; Chongshan Liao
abstract:
Adenoid hypertrophy (AH) is common in children and causes upper airway obstruction, which frequently forces oral breathing. In this study, we developed a deep learning framework (AH_KNet) to automatically identify AH and assess its severity using lateral cephalograms, with the aim of providing an objective, non-invasive aid for screening and referral in routine practice.
A cohort of 1,499 lateral cephalograms (899 normal, 600 AH) was collected and divided into training (n = 1,337) and test (n = 162) datasets. A validation subset (n = 162) was randomly extracted from the training set for hyperparameter tuning and internal evaluation. We used a ResNet-50 backbone with a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) to regress anatomical landmarks and calculate the Adenoidal/Nasopharyngeal (A/N) ratio. To improve robustness, landmark optimization strategy (Method B) was implemented by excluding the unstable Articulare (Ar) point. Statistics included intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs), mean radial error (MRE), F-value, p-value, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, Cohen's kappa, and Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.
The proposed approach AH_KNet achieved high reliability in landmark detection (peak ICC = 0.991). Compared with the conventional method, performance improved across multiple metrics: accuracy increased from 90.26% to 93.80%, Cohen's kappa from 69.84% to 80.06%, and Area Under the Curve (AUC) from 0.865 to 0.913. Inference time was under one second per image, supporting efficient integration into clinical workflows.
This AI-assisted model offers potential in supporting opportunistic screening pediatric AH. By providing rapid and consistent radiographic assessment, it may assist orthodontists in identifying children who require further otolaryngologic evaluation, while maintaining current diagnostic workflows.

title: Fragmentia-AI lymphoma: a cfDNA language model for lymphoma detection using ultra-low-pass WGS.
authors: Yang Dai; Xushu Zhong; Hua Bao; Xinghan Sun; Guofeng Sun; Ke Xu; Yang Xu; Liyan Guo; Qian Hu; Qiaolin Zhou; Xu Sun; He Li; Jie Wang; Jinrong Yang; Yijun Wu; Ailin Zhao; Liuqing Zhu; Xue Wu; Yang Shao; Ting Niu
abstract: Lymphomas are biologically and clinically heterogeneous malignancies. While liquid biopsies using circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) offer a non-invasive alternative, current methods typically require expensive deep sequencing. We developed Fragmentia-AI™ Lymphoma, a transformer-based genomic language model that enables lymphoma detection using ultra-low-pass whole-genome sequencing (ULP-WGS). The model integrates a genomic language model backbone with attention-based multiple instance learning to identify mutation-independent, malignancy-associated signals directly from raw cfDNA sequences. The model was trained on 389 samples (189 lymphoma, 200 healthy) and evaluated in an independent validation cohort of 190 lymphoma patients and 200 healthy controls. The model demonstrated robust diagnostic performance in the validation cohort, achieving an AUC of 0.944, with a sensitivity of 0.842 at 98% specificity and an F1 score of 0.904. Read-depth titration analysis showed sustained performance at sequencing depths as low as 0.01x, representing a substantial reduction compared with standard cfDNA mutation-based approaches. Attention-based fragment prioritization indicated that predictions were driven by fragmentomic signatures, including GC-content bias and altered fragment-size distributions characteristic of malignant cfDNA. These findings support the feasibility of a mutation-independent approach that may inform future lymphoma detection and monitoring strategies.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Behavioral Phenotyping: From Behavioral Neuroscience to Depression Research.
authors: Carina Soares-Cunha
abstract: Behavioral phenotyping remains the main experimental readout for investigating brain function and neuropsychiatric disease. However, conventional behavioral analysis relies largely on manually defined endpoints that simplify the multidimensional nature of behavior and often overlook subtle behavioral dynamics. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL) and computer vision, are fundamentally transforming this landscape by enabling automated, high-resolution quantification of behavior across species and experimental paradigms. This review discusses recent developments in AI-based behavioral phenotyping and their implications for translational neuroscience, with particular emphasis on emerging applications to depression research. We first describe how markerless pose estimation has changed movement quantification, followed by supervised and unsupervised ML approaches that classify predefined behaviors or discover latent behavioral motifs directly from movement data. We then discuss how these approaches are reshaping systems neuroscience by enabling increasingly detailed descriptions of behavioral organization and facilitating the investigation of behavior as a continuous, multidimensional process. Finally, we examine their application to experimental models and clinical studies of depression, considering their potential and the limitations of translating computational behavioral measures across experimental and clinical settings. AI-based behavioral phenotyping represents an important methodological advance in neuroscience, shifting behavioral analysis from the quantification of isolated experimental endpoints toward the characterization of integrated behavioral states. In depression research, these approaches may improve behavioral characterization in experimental models and provide quantitative measures of clinically-relevant behavioral alterations in humans. However, linking experimental and clinical phenotypes will require methodological standardization, independent validation, and careful evaluation of cross-species comparability.

title: Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
authors: Katane Elizabeth Kekana; Thokozani Isaac Mtshali
journal: Journal of Education and Learning Technology
abstract: Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.
