title: Accuracy of suprasternal ultrasonography compared with fluoroscopy for assessing endotracheal tube depth in preschool children with congenital heart disease
authors: Ornin Chintabanyat; Pornnapat Konateerakul; Pichaya Waitayawinyu; Chodchanok Vijarnsorn; Kasana Raksamani
abstract: Endotracheal tube (ETT) malposition may occur in children with congenital heart disease because of shorter tracheal length and growth restriction. This prospective diagnostic accuracy study evaluated suprasternal ultrasonography for confirming ETT depth in 116 preschool children (0–6 years) undergoing elective cardiac catheterization under general anesthesia. Microcuff ETTs were inserted using the vocal cord depth mark. Ultrasonographic visualization of the cuff at the suprasternal notch (SSN), a prespecified surrogate for correct tip position, was compared with fluoroscopic tip position as the reference standard. Fluoroscopy showed correct tip position in 99 patients (85.3%). Using cuff visualization at the SSN as the criterion, sensitivity was 40.4% (95% CI, 30.7–50.7), specificity 70.6% (95% CI, 44.0–89.7), and overall agreement 44.8%, with negligible agreement beyond chance. In post hoc exploratory analyses, extending the threshold to 1.1–1.3 cm above the SSN increased sensitivity to above 80% but reduced specificity to 20%. The size-dependent distance between the cuff and the tube tip may explain part of this discordance. The SSN-based cuff criterion has limited accuracy for confirming ETT depth in this population and should not be used alone; revised ultrasonographic criteria require prospective validation. Clinical trial registration The study was registered in the Thai Clinical Trials Registry before data collection process (TCTR20230218001).

title: Hemodynamic effects of cycle ergometry versus dynamic unilateral arm exercise during right heart catheterization: a prospective observational study
authors: Eugen Berezucki; Maria Heinrich; Alexander Rueß; Tobias J. Lange; Markus Perl; Stefan Stadler
abstract: BACKGROUND: The reintroduction of exercise pulmonary hypertension (EPH) to the pulmonary hypertension (PH) definition by the European guidelines underlines the importance of examining the hemodynamic response to exercise during right heart catheterization. Because the standard exercise modality of cycle ergometry (CE) is not universally accessible, we compared its hemodynamic effects with those of dynamic single-arm exercise (AE) in patients undergoing right heart catheterization (RHC). METHODS: 50 consecutive patients with indication for RHC were enrolled. Hemodynamic parameters were assessed at rest, followed by randomized exercise periods with an intervening rest phase. Thermodilution was used to determine cardiac output. The intensity of the AE was patient-determined, whereas CE was conducted at a fixed work rate ranging from 10 to 50 watts, based on the patient's physical status. Oxygen uptake (VO₂) was estimated using the reverse Fick principle to compare relative exercise intensity between modalities. EPH was defined by an mPAP/cardiac output slope > 3 mmHg·L⁻¹·min⁻¹, and exercise-induced left heart disease by a rise in PAWP from ≤ 15 mmHg at rest to > 25 mmHg during exercise. RESULTS: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure increased by 12 mmHg with CE compared to 3 mmHg with AE (p<0.001), pulmonary artery wedge pressure increased by 5 mmHg versus 2 mmHg (p<0.001), cardiac output increased by 2.2 L/min versus 0.6 L/min (p<0.001) and mean pulmonary vascular resistance decreased by 0.05 WU with CE (p=0.761) and by 0.32 with AE (p=0.03). Estimated VO₂ during AE reached only 24% of the increase observed during CE, corresponding to an external workload equivalent of approximately 6 W. No patient showed an increase in pulmonary artery wedge pressure during exercise above 25mmHg to unmask left heart disease. In patients without PH at rest, CE led to the diagnosis of EPH in 5 patients while the used AE protocol was not suitable to detect EPH. CONCLUSION: AE proved to be a safe exercise modality in our study but, with the protocol applied here, produced significantly smaller hemodynamic changes during RHC than CE and is thus not an adequate substitute in this form, leaving open whether an intensity-matched protocol could achieve comparable hemodynamic effects.

title: Association of Site Volume and MitraClip Outcomes in Secondary Mitral Regurgitation
authors: Kashish Goel; Raj R. Makkar; Hursh Naik; Satya Atmakuri; Paul Mahoney; M. Andrew Morse; Janani Aiyer; Rong Huang; Vinod H. Thourani; JoAnn Lindenfeld; Brian R. Lindman; Colin Barker
abstract: BACKGROUND: The number of sites performing transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) for secondary mitral regurgitation (SMR) has increased. Despite concerns that low-volume sites may have worse outcomes, data are limited on the association between site volume and TEER outcomes. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the association between site volume and mitral TEER outcomes in SMR. METHODS: The COAPT PAS (COAPT Post-Approval Study) included patients with SMR who underwent TEER with the MitraClip device from March 2019 to September 2020 following Food and Drug Administration approval. Sites were categorized by number of patients treated: low (≤25), medium (25-50), and high (>50). RESULTS: Of 5,000 patients, 2,632 were from low-, 1,527 from medium-, and 841 from high-volume sites. High-volume sites treated sicker patients with higher Society of Thoracic Surgeons scores and prior heart failure hospitalization rates. Procedures at low-volume sites had similar device implant rates (low: 97%, medium: 99%, high: 98%), used fewer number of clips (low: 1.4 ± 0.6, medium: 1.5 ± 0.6, high: 1.6 ± 0.7 clips, P < 0.001), and had longer device (low: 68 ± 55, medium: 56 ± 53, high: 57 ± 42 min, P < 0.001) and procedure times (low: 153 ± 67, medium: 131 ± 59, high: 128 ± 56 min, P < 0.001). Technical success was comparable (low: 93%, medium: 94%, high: 95%, P = 0.92). MR reduction to ≤2+ and ≤1+ was also similar. There was no difference in heart failure hospitalization (low: 19%, medium: 18%, high: 20%, P = 0.50) or all-cause mortality (low: 23%, medium: 21%, high: 20%, P = 0.27). CONCLUSIONS: Technical success, MR reduction, and 1-year clinical outcomes were comparable across volume strata during the early adoption phase, without significant differences between low- and high-volume centers.

title: Biventricular Reverse Remodeling After Percutaneous Pulmonary Valve Implantation With a Self-Expandable Pulsta Valve in Native Right Ventricular Outflow Tract
authors: Woo Young Park; Gi Beom Kim; Sang Yun Lee; M K Song; Seung Min Baek; Susan Taejung Kim; Duck Woo Lee; Eun Jung Bae
abstract: Background: The effects of percutaneous pulmonary valve implantation (PPVI) on biventricular remodeling, ventricular interaction, and effective right ventricular (RV) forward flow in native RV outflow tract disease remain incompletely characterized.

title: Double-Outlet Left Atrium in a One-Month-Old Boy: A Rare Heart Anomaly in a Resource-Limited Setting
authors: Aisha Nakato; Emma Tina Ndagire; Hilda Tumwebaze; Gloria Owomugisha; Twalib Olega Aliku; Sulaiman Lubega
abstract: Double-outlet left atrium (DOLA) is an exceedingly rare congenital cardiac anomaly caused by ventriculoatrial malalignment.Its presentation ranges from subtle cyanosis to delayed manifestations resembling an atrial septal defect.We report a one-month-old male infant who presented with cyanosis and symptoms of heart failure.Echocardiography showed a rare variant of double-outlet atrium, in which the right atrium emptied solely through a patent foramen ovale (PFO) into the left atrium, which drained into both ventricles through a common atrioventricular (AV) valve.Treatment with intravenous furosemide and supplemental oxygen did not produce significant improvement.He was too unstable for surgical intervention, deteriorated, and died three days after diagnosis.The presumed cause of death was refractory heart failure or an arrhythmia.His parents declined a postmortem examination, so pathological confirmation was not possible.This case illustrates the diagnostic challenges of DOLA, which can mimic a complete AV canal defect, and shows that careful echocardiographic assessment of the AV junction is key to diagnosis.Clinical instability at diagnosis limited surgical options in our patient, highlighting the potential value of early fetal and neonatal cardiac screening.

title: Restoration of sinus rhythm after mitral valve plasty with concomitant left atrial appendage excision in four small-breed dogs with myxomatous mitral valve disease and atrial fibrillation: a case series
authors: Tomoki Wada; Takuya Mori; Ryosuke TAKEMURA; Hideki Yotsuida
abstract: Four dogs with mitral regurgitation (MR) secondary to myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) were referred for mitral valve plasty (MVP). Electrocardiography revealed the absence of P waves and irregular RR intervals in all dogs, confirming atrial fibrillation (AF). Echocardiography showed mitral valve prolapse with regurgitation and enlargement of the left atrium (LA) and left ventricle. All dogs underwent MVP under cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) with chordal reconstruction and annuloplasty, combined with left atrial appendage (LAA) excision as an adjunctive procedure to address potential LAA blood stasis, thrombus formation, and arrhythmogenic substrate. Postoperatively, episodes of AF or other supraventricular tachyarrhythmias occurred in all dogs; however, sinus rhythm (SR) was restored in all dogs and was documented on follow-up surface electrocardiograms (ECGs) more than 1 year after surgery, although AF later recurred in one dog. LA size decreased after surgery, although LA enlargement persisted at 3 months. These cases illustrate the postoperative rhythm changes following MVP with concomitant LAA excision and highlight the importance of longitudinal rhythm assessment. Larger comparative studies with systematic rhythm monitoring are needed to evaluate postoperative rhythm outcomes and the contributions of the individual procedures. Moreover, because all four dogs weighed less than 10 kg, these findings cannot be generalized to medium- and large-sized dogs.

title: Flash pulmonary edema immediately after cavotricuspid isthmus ablation for typical atrial flutter: a case report
authors: Yufei Xu; Meng Wang; Xiaoqing Liu
abstract: With the accelerating aging of the population, the incidence of atrial flutter has continued to rise, and catheter ablation has been recommended by guidelines as an effective treatment strategy for atrial flutter. Flash pulmonary edema is a rare but life-threatening complication whose exact mechanism remains unclear, and previous reports have mostly involved electrical cardioversion or atrial fibrillation ablation. Here, we report a rare case of flash pulmonary edema occurring immediately after cavotricuspid isthmus ablation in a patient with atrial flutter, with the aim of providing a reference for clinical diagnosis and treatment. A 78-year-old man with chronic heart failure, severe mitral regurgitation, silicosis, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease underwent catheter ablation for cavotricuspid isthmus-dependent atrial flutter. Upon completion of ablation, he suddenly developed flash pulmonary edema complicated by type II respiratory failure. His dyspnea improved rapidly after afterload reduction and diuresis, but hypoxemia persisted; noninvasive ventilation was started on his return to the ward approximately 2 h after onset, after which SpO₂ increased gradually to 90%, and he was discharged on postoperative day 7. At 1-month follow-up, high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) and the electrocardiogram had returned to normal, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) had decreased markedly; echocardiography showed that mitral regurgitation had decreased from severe to mild-to-moderate. Flash pulmonary edema can also occur immediately after isolated cavotricuspid isthmus ablation in patients with typical atrial flutter. In high-risk patients with poor cardiopulmonary reserve and concomitant mitral regurgitation, early recognition, rapid reduction of cardiac preload and afterload, and early respiratory support, including noninvasive ventilation as soon as respiratory failure is recognized, may be key to improving prognosis.

title: Multiorgan failure in a young patient with necrotizing fasciitis: a case report of septic shock progressing to mixed shock with fatal cardiac outcome
authors: Richard F. Kraus; Christina K. Kaufmann; Volker Alt; Martin G. Kees
abstract: BACKGROUND: Necrotizing soft tissue infections (NSTIs) are rare, life-threatening conditions requiring immediate and aggressive treatment. Despite advances in medical care, mortality remains high, largely due to septic shock and severe complications. CASE REPRESENTATION: We report the case of a young adult with necrotizing fasciitis (NF) of the left leg complicated by recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding and infective endocarditis, resulting in severe heart failure and ultimately leading to death. The fatal outcome was most likely attributable to prolonged sepsis with multiorgan involve- and impairment and a 1.5-cm paravalvular abscess caused by vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium. CONCLUSION: The treatment of a septic patient with progressive heart failure highlights the value of an integrative, multidisciplinary approach to complex clinical decision-making and the real-world challenges that may require patient-tailored, nonstandard therapeutic strategies. Prompt diagnosis, aggressive surgical debridement, and rigorous management of complications are essential. In cases of aortic valve regurgitation causing heart failure, TAVI implantation might serve as a temporary bridge until definitive open valve replacement becomes feasible.

title: Predictors of naive functional mitral regurgitation progression after isolated correction of chronic aortic regurgitation
authors: A.A. Bulynin; Eduard R Charchyan; Sergey O. Popov
abstract: Objective. To identify predictors of naive functional mitral regurgitation (MR) progression in patients with severe left ventricular dilatation after isolated correction of aortic valve disease. Material and methods. The study included 80 patients with left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) ≥ 250 ml due to chronic AI with functional MR. In all patients, AI was the only primary factor of left ventricular remodeling. Surgical treatment of AI was performed using the David and Bentall-DeBono techniques, as well as aortic valve replacement and isolated aortic valve leaflet repair. Functional MR was assessed using transthoracic echocardiography. We evaluated MR and potential predictors 1—10 days before surgery, 7—10 days after surgery, and at least 6 months after surgical treatment. Results. Preoperative mitral annulus diameter (MAD) ≥ 45 mm is an independent predictor of long-term MR progression with LVEDV ≥ 250 ml in all groups with (OR 1.560, CI 1.033—2.358, p=0.035). The MAD/left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD) ratio ≥ 0.539 before surgery is a significant predictor of postoperative MR progression (AUC=0.734; 95% CI: 0.562—0.905, p=0.011). The MAD/left ventricular end-systolic diameter (LVESD) ratio ≥ 0.833 before surgery is a significant predictor of MR progression (AUC=0.698; 95% CI: 0.522—0.875, p=0.031). Conclusion. Functional MR following chronic AI may progress after correction of aortic valve disease in patients with severe mitral annular dilatation.

title: Modified robotic atrial septal defect repair on beating heart: a nine-year single-centre experience with learning-curve analysis and comparison with thoracoscopy
authors: Hanchao Feng; Mingke Li; JinMo Kong; Yawei Dai; 吴延虎; Yihu Tang
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate a modified robot-assisted technique for atrial septal defect (ASD) repair on beating heart and to compare perioperative outcomes with thoracoscopic repair. Methods 198 patients with ASD underwent modified ASD repair using the Da Vinci robotic surgical system on beating heart in the Department of Cardiovascular Surgery of the First Affiliated Hospital with Nanjing Medical University. Cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis was used to build learning curves for operation time and cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) time. Patients operated after both curves had plateaued formed the robotic group (n = 117); 113 patients treated thoracoscopically during the same period served as the comparison group. Results The learning curves for operation time and CPB time were 81 cases and 66 cases respectively. ASD diameter and pulmonary artery systolic pressure were higher in the robotic group, which also contained seven patients with partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection (PAPVC) and one with anomalous drainage of the inferior vena cava. CPB time was shorter in the robotic group. Operation time, mechanical ventilation time, intensive care unit stay, postoperative hospital stay and 24-hour chest drainage did not differ. Echocardiography at 3, 30 and 90 days and at one year showed no residual shunt or tricuspid regurgitation in either group. Conclusions The modified robot-assisted technique for beating-heart ASD repair is safe and reproducible. Once the learning curve is complete, CPB time is shorter than with thoracoscopy despite greater anatomical complexity, and the technique offers a valid minimally invasive option for defects that are unsuitable for device closure.

title: Acute severe mitral and aortic regurgitation associated with adult-onset Still’s disease
authors: Wafa Baya; Wiem Romdhane; N. Adaily; Imen Ben Hassine; J. Anoun; Amel Rezgui; F. Ben Fredj Ismail
journal: European Journal of Case Reports in Internal Medicine
abstract: Background: Adult-onset Still’s disease (AOSD) is a rare systemic inflammatory disease of unknown etiology usually affecting young adults. The primary clinical features are fever, rash, and arthritis or arthralgia. Cardiac involvement, especially valvular regurgitation, is less common. Only three cases of severe aortic and/or mitral regurgitation associated with AOSD have been reported. Case Report: A 25-year-old man presented with fever evolving for 15 days, recent exertional dyspnea and diffuse arthromyalgia. On examination, the patient had a body temperature of 39.5°C and a pansystolic murmur at the mitral area radiating to the axilla and an early diastolic decrescendo murmur at the left sternal border with a modest intensity on cardiac auscultation. Laboratory tests revealed important leukocytosis with a predominance of neutrophils. Initial cardiac echocardiography ruled out infectious endocarditis, and revealed valvular dilated heart disease with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction with severe aortic and mitral regurgitation and a minimal tricuspid insufficiency. Pericarditis occurred secondarily. The evolution was marked by the onset of an acute left ventricular insufficiency and worsening of the pericarditis requiring a diuretic. The patient was diagnosed with AOSD using Yamaguchi’s classification criteria. He was started on 1 mg/kg/d corticosteroid therapy, and scheduled for double valve replacement. A good outcome was achieved. Conclusion: It is paramount to identify all the clinical manifestations of AOSD with a systematic screening for cardiac involvement especially when the patient presents with discrete symptoms such as exertional dyspnea. Thereby, early diagnosis and adequate treatment reduce the disease’s critical complications.

title: Higher left atrial volumetric/mechanical coupling index is associated with postoperative adverse events in significant aortic regurgitation
authors: Na Chen; Siqi Cao; Huiyu Tang; Wenhui Gu; Siyao Sun; Qiwu Sun; Tao Cong; Haibo Wu; Jun Wu
abstract: Background The role of left atrial volumetric/mechanical coupling index (LACI) in significant aortic regurgitation (AR) remains unclear. Objective This study aimed to clarify the relationship between LACI and postoperative adverse events in significant AR. Methods This dual-center retrospective cohort comprised 248 patients with significant AR who underwent aortic valve replacement (AVR) from December 2019 to June 2025. LACI was obtained by dividing maximal left atrial volume index by septal mitral annular late diastolic velocity (a′). Patients were stratified by the median LACI value (5.9). The composite primary endpoint was cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure. Associations between LACI and clinical outcomes were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. The incremental prognostic value of LACI was evaluated by concordance index (C-index), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and net reclassification improvement (NRI), with internal validation performed using 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed to confirm the robustness of findings. Results During a median follow-up of 27.3 (IQR, 17.2–36.7) months, 52 (21.9%) patients experienced the composite primary endpoint. Kaplan–Meier analysis demonstrated significantly higher event-free survival in the LACI <5.9 group (log-rank P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, higher LACI remained independently associated with the primary endpoint (adjustedHR 1.096, 95% CI 1.053–1.141, P < 0.001), with each additional unit raising event risk by 9.6%. Receiver operating characteristic analysis indicated that LACI had an area under the curve of 0.738. C-index, IDI, and NRI confirmed that LACI added incremental prognostic information to the core parameters recommended by current guidelines. Conclusion Higher LACI was independently associated with worse postoperative outcomes in patients with significant AR. LACI may add incremental prognostic information to the core parameters recommended by current guidelines.

title: Midterm outcomes of mitral valve replacement in children: a retrospective study
authors: Rixin Liang; Canxin Wang; Jing Ling; Jiaxiong Wu; Zirui Peng; Jinxin Li; Haiyun Yuan; Shusheng Wen
abstract: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the midterm outcomes of mitral valve replacement (MVR) in children aged 1–18 years with irreparable mitral valve disease. Methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of patients who underwent MVR at our institution between January 2010 and December 2025. We excluded patients who underwent valve repair or were outside the age range. We collected and analyzed preoperative, intraoperative, postoperative, and follow-up data for the enrolled pediatric patients. Results A total of 89 patients were enrolled in this study, including 41 males and 48 females, with a median age of 9.0 years (IQR 4.0–14.0). Median weight and body surface area were 24.8 kg (IQR 13.5, 38.6) and 0.9 m 2 (IQR 0.6–1.3), respectively. The preoperative diagnoses included mitral stenosis in 31 patients (34.8%), mitral regurgitation in 78 patients (87.6%), and combined mitral stenosis and regurgitation in 20 patients (22.5%). A subset of patients had associated anomalies, including complete atrioventricular septal defect, partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection, and congenital mitral valve malformations. All 89 patients successfully underwent the procedure. The operative time was 310.3 ± 96.4 min, cardiopulmonary bypass time was 177.2 ± 72.5 min, and aortic cross-clamp time was 102.5 ± 44.3 min. Postoperative mechanical ventilation duration was 21.0 h (IQR 10.0–36.9), ICU stay was 3.0 days (IQR 2.0–6.3), and hospital length of stay was 26.0 days (IQR 18.8–37.5). A total of 34 patients (38.2%) underwent implantation with a 25# valve, 24 patients (27.0%) with a 27# valve, and 11 patients (12.4%) with a 23# valve. At a median follow-up of 24.5 months (IQR 7.0, 69.0), crude overall survival was 98.9% (88/89). Conclusion MVR represents a feasible and safe treatment strategy for children with irreparable mitral valve lesions, demonstrating excellent midterm survival and low complication rates in this cohort.

title: Maternal outcomes of infective endocarditis in pregnancy: a narrative review of diagnosis and multidisciplinary management
authors: Nishat Altaf Deraiya; Safa Pathan; Sancia Raymond Selwyn; Shiaaneish Arumugam; Yashgauri Wagh; Blessy Kongasseri
journal: International Journal of Reproduction Contraception Obstetrics and Gynecology
abstract: Infective endocarditis (IE) in pregnancy is rare (incidence about 0.006%) but increasing, driven by injection drug use, prosthetic valves and cardiac devices, and more women with congenital heart disease reaching reproductive age. Pregnancy obscures presentation and constrains diagnosis and treatment, and the evidence is scattered across case reports, small series and retrospective cohorts. This narrative review synthesizes published case reports, case series, cohort studies and reviews on IE in pregnancy and the postpartum period, focusing on maternal outcomes, risk factors, diagnosis and management, with fetal outcomes as a secondary consideration. Risk factors include injection drug use, rheumatic and congenital heart disease, prosthetic valves and intracardiac devices; Staphylococcus aureus predominates. Physiological murmurs, atypical symptoms and other febrile illnesses delay diagnosis. Contemporary maternal in-hospital mortality is 5-17% and, in the two largest comparative datasets, did not differ significantly from that of non-pregnant women. IE diagnosed during the delivery admission is the exception, with 17.2% mortality and severe morbidity in 77.5%. Heart failure, septic embolization and arrhythmia dominate morbidity. Valve surgery rates are similar to those in non-pregnant patients; bypass during pregnancy yields excellent maternal survival but 18-20% fetal mortality, favoring cesarean delivery followed by valve surgery once the fetus is viable. Multidisciplinary care, including addiction medicine, was associated with fewer patient-directed discharges. IE in pregnancy mainly alters recognition and management rather than survival of established disease, except at delivery. Early suspicion, echocardiography, blood cultures, pregnancy-compatible antimicrobials, timing of delivery and surgery, and tertiary multidisciplinary care are central. Prospective registries are needed.

title: Cardiac Involvement in Storage Disorders: Pathophysiology, Multimodality Diagnosis, and Emerging Disease-Modifying Therapies
authors: L. Jacqueline
abstract: Cardiac involvement is a major determinant of morbidity and mortality in storage disorders, including Fabry disease, Pompe disease, Danon disease, PRKAG2 syndrome, transthyretin and light-chain amyloidosis, the mucopolysaccharidoses, Gaucher disease, and Niemann-Pick disease. Because their cardiac phenotype mimics hypertensive heart disease, athlete's heart, and sarcomeric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, these conditions are often recognised only after irreversible myocardial fibrosis has developed, when disease-specific therapy is least effective. This narrative review aims to summarise the pathophysiology, disease-specific phenotypes, multimodality imaging, molecular diagnosis, and current and emerging treatment of storage cardiomyopathies, framed around the clinical problem of unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy and restrictive physiology. Relevant literature was identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by hand-searching of guidelines and consensus statements, with priority given to randomised trials, registries, and expert consensus. Although their upstream biology differs, storage cardiomyopathies converge on common pathways of substrate accumulation, lysosomal and mitochondrial dysfunction, fibrosis, and electrical instability. Native T1 and T2 mapping, extracellular volume quantification, late gadolinium enhancement, strain echocardiography, and bone scintigraphy now permit earlier and more specific diagnosis. Enzyme replacement therapy, pharmacological chaperones, transthyretin stabilisers, and RNA-targeted agents are most effective when started before fibrosis is established, whereas gene replacement and genome editing remain investigational. Early recognition through structured multimodality imaging and molecular diagnosis, combined with multidisciplinary care, is essential to ensure timely disease-specific therapy and improve long-term outcomes.

title: Forward Stroke Volume and Ejection Fraction Estimation in Mitral Regurgitation: A Computational Hemodynamic Approach
authors: Amirahmad Saeidi; Mobina Ghajar; Sara Tarkiani; Amin Ramezani
abstract: Mitral regurgitation (MR) is a common valvular heart disease in which con- ventional measures such as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) can be misleading, as they do not distinguish between effective forward flow and regurgitant volume. This limitation may result in underestimation of the true hemodynamic burden of the disease. In this study, we develop a computational framework based on a closed-loop lumped-parameter cardiovascular model to evaluate forward cardiac function in MR. The model incorporates a regurgitant pathway across the mitral valve together with flow calculations at the left ventric- ular outflow tract (LVOT), allowing estimation of forward stroke volume (FSV) and forward ejection fraction (FEF).The model was first assessed against published physiological reference values and then used to simulate different levels of mitral leakage. As simulated regurgitant fraction increased from 0% to 58.30%, FSV decreased from 65.35 to 51.37 mL and FEF from 60.22% to 35.21%, while LVEF increased from 60.17% to 84.40%. These results illustrate how increased LVEF can coexist with reduced forward output in modeled MR. Overall, the proposed approach provides a physiologically interpretable and computationally efficient tool for analyzing MR hemodynamics. The framework provides a research tool for investigating MR hemodynamics and compar- ing conventional and forward-flow-based measures. Further validation using patient-specific clinical data is required before it can be considered for clinical application.

title: Cellular and molecular mechanisms of arrhythmogenesis in Takotsubo syndrome (Review)
authors: Danqi Xu; Xuan Chen; Maolin Hao; XU Qianqian; Binbin Zhao; Wenjun Huang; Xiaobo Zhou; Qiang Xu; Huan Lan
abstract: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), an acute stress‑induced heart failure, is frequently complicated by arrhythmias that significantly worsen prognosis. Despite advances in understanding its pathology, the electrophysiological basis of these arrhythmias remains incompletely elucidated. The present review synthesizes current evidence to explore the core electrophysiological mechanisms underlying arrhythmogenesis in TTS, including abnormal calcium handling, repolarization abnormalities, altered conduction and refractoriness due to structural remodelling, and autonomic nervous system imbalance. The corresponding clinical manifestations of ventricular arrhythmias, atrial arrhythmias and bradyarrhythmias were further delineated, and contemporary diagnostic and therapeutic strategies were discussed. By integrating clinical observations with experimental findings, the present review aims to bridge the knowledge gap between mechanistic insights and clinical practice. Finally, critical research gaps were highlighted and future directions were proposed, emphasizing the need for personalized medicine and novel therapeutic targets to improve arrhythmia management and patient outcomes in TTS.

title: 3D bioprinting of tissues and organs for systemic diseases and localized injuries
authors: W. Kee Ng; Paulo Bártolo
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting integrates engineering, materials science, and biology to fabricate living tissues with precise spatial control. By enabling the layer-by-layer deposition of cells and biomaterials, it overcomes many limitations of traditional scaffold-based tissue engineering and offers new opportunities for regenerative and personalized medicine. This review presents a comprehensive overview of recent advances in 3D bioprinting. It introduces a systematic, ASTM-aligned classification of key bioprinting modalities, extrusion, jetting, and vat photopolymerization, along with their respective material and biological design requirements. It also summarizes recent progress in bio-ink development and crosslinking strategies that improve print fidelity and functional tissue maturation. In addition, the review highlights applications in both systemic disease modelling and treatment (such as cardiovascular, endocrine/metabolic, and neurodegenerative disorders) and localized tissue repair (including skin, musculoskeletal, cartilage, and bone), emphasizing their relevance to civilian healthcare and military medicine. By combining technological innovation, biological insights, and regulatory considerations, this review outlines how advances in multi-modal bioprinting and intelligent process control can accelerate the translation of laboratory research into clinically viable, patient-specific therapies, driving the next generation of regenerative medicine.

title: Artificial intelligence driven software systems for cardiovascular disease detection using physiological signals: a systematic review
authors: MD Tasnim Alam; Abdullah Al-Mamun Bulbul; Md Ismail Hossen; A. K. M. Azad; Asaduzzaman Khan; Mohammad Ali Moni
abstract: Abstract Cardiovascular disease exacts an extraordinary global toll, with annual mortality exceeding 17.9 million lives and representing nearly one-third of all deaths worldwide. Reducing diagnostic delays, particularly in resource-limited settings, requires innovative, scalable, and cost-effective solutions. Artificial intelligence integrated with physiological signals, such as electrocardiogram (ECG), photoplethysmogram (PPG) and phonocardiogram (PCG), offers promising pathways for scalable, real-time cardiovascular assessment. Despite rapid advances, the evidence base remains fragmented, impeding identification of validated approaches and clinical translation pathways. A PRISMA-guided search across five databases (Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, Embase, IEEE Xplore) identified 35 eligible peer-reviewed studies. Quality and risk of bias were appraised using a QUADAS-2 adapted framework. Most systems utilised ECG (71.4%) with deep learning architectures, including convolutional and recurrent neural networks. Critical gaps were quantified: only 23% of studies conducted external validation, only 14% achieved clinical-scale deployment, no study integrated principled multi-signal fusion (ECG + PPG + PCG), and only one system (1/35, 2.9%) implemented a patient-facing conversational interface. Reported accuracies ranged from 70.5 to 99.9% (n = 21 reporting; unweighted mean 93.7%), but inconsistent metric reporting and limited external validation tempered translational confidence. A three-directional framework is proposed, addressing generalisability through multi-signal (ECG + PPG + PCG) models, interpretability through LLM-driven clinical narratives, and accessibility through edge-cloud deployment, to guide future research toward clinically deployable systems.

title: Nonvalvular atrial fibrillation during chronic stress in the context of war in Ukraine: integrating mental health, pathophysiology, and pharmacotherapy in to a future-oriented model of care
authors: Марина Миколаївна Долженко; Наталя Анатоліївна Білоусова; V. Nesukai; Nataliia Kozhuharyova; L. Ye. Lobach; L. Konoplianyk; T. V. Mahanova; Наталя Олександрівна Ткаченко
abstract: Mental health disorders resulting from war-related stress may interact with cardiovascular risk factors, highlighting the importance of understanding the course of nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (nAF) and the organization of medical care in resource-limited settings. Objective To analyze evidence-based medicine (EBM) data on the mutual influence of atrial fibrillation (AF), chronic psychosocial stress, and mental health disorders with subsequent modeling of a future-oriented conceptual model of integrated patient-centered medical care for patients with nAF in wartime and post-war reconstruction of the Healthcare system in Ukraine. Methods A narrative review of EBM data on epidemiological trends, pathophysiology of nAF, mental health, pharmacotherapy, Drug-Drug Interactions (DDI), patient-oriented, and digital interventions was conducted. Results The relationships of psycho-emotional, cardiometabolic, behavioral and socioeconomic factors with the risk of onset and course of nAF were identified. Potential common mechanisms are dysregulation of the autonomic and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal systems, inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction and atrial remodeling. Mental health disorders can affect symptom burden, adherence to treatment, quality of life and safety of pharmacotherapy. A future-oriented conceptual integrated multidisciplinary model of Healthcare system was modeled. Conclusions The analyzed data confirm the associative biopsychosocial links of nAF in conditions of chronic stress, but do not allow us to unambiguously establish the causal effect of chronic war stress on the development and progression of nAF. A future-oriented integrated conceptual model can be the basis for adapting medical care to war conditions and the post-war period in Healthcare system.

title: Atrial Fibrillation During Zanubrutinib Treatment in Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia With a Historical Ibrutinib Control
authors: Andrea Visentin; Enrica Antonia Martino; Alessandro Cellini; Francesco Angotzi; Annalisa Pitino; Andrea Duminuco; Ernesto Vigna; Raffaella Pasquale; Isacco Ferrarini; Riccardo Moia; Alessandro Sanna; Marina Motta; Massimo Moratti; Paolo Sportoletti; Annalisa Chiarenza; Alessandro Maggi; Valentina Zammit; Michele Merli; Idanna Innocenti; Claudia Giordano; Laura Nocilli; Massimiliano Postorino; Caterina Stelitano; Andrea Ferrario; Anna Maria Frustaci; Marcello Riva; Sara Pepe; Adalberto Ibatici; Stefania Scardino; Paola Anticoli Borza; Laura Ballotta; Salvatrice Mancuso; Francesco Malaspina; Anna Mele; Sara Galimberti; Gioacchino Catania; Annamaria Giordano; Ilaria Angeletti; Luana Schiattone; Elsa Pennese; Rosanna Miccolis; Angelo Famà; Giulio Giordano; Catello Califano; Antonella Bruzzese; Giuliana Farina; Pietro Bulian; Giacomo Loseto; Barbara Pocali; Vanessa Innao; Piero Galieni; Vincenzo Fraticelli; Candida Vitale; Azzurra Romeo; Marco Rossi; Ilaria Scortechini; Federico Vozella; Luigi Malandruccolo; Marzia Varettoni; Lucia Morello; Giuseppe Pietrantuono; Esmeralda Conte; Martina Cantelli; Roberta Murru; Daniele Caracciolo; Enrico Derenzini; Valentina Di Martina; Roberto Marasca; Maria Ilaria Del Principe; Amalia Figuera; Marta Coscia; Nicola Di Renzo; Luca Laurenti; Nicola Amodio; Alessandro Allegra; Vittorio Del Fabro; Paolo Fiumara; Luca Scalise; Fabio Stagno; Giorgio Tona; P Musto; Laura Caruso; Arcangelo Liso; Alessandra Tedeschi; Gianluca Gaidano; Francesca Romana Mauro; Giovanni Tripepi; Fortunato Morabito; Giuseppe Alberto Palumbo; Francesco Di Raimondo; Valter Gattei; Livio Trentin; Massimo Gentile
abstract: Introduction: Atrial fibrillation (AF) complicates Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy in chronic lymphocytic leukemia. Methods: We retrospectively evaluated 679 zanubrutinib-treated patients across 52 Italian centers, with 354 historical ibrutinib-treated controls. Shanafelt AF scores were assessed. Results: Nine zanubrutinib-treated patients developed AF (1.33%) during median treatment of 15.5 months, versus 42 historical controls (11.9%) over median observation of 25 months. Five zanubrutinib events occurred among patients scoring ≥ 5. No affected patients experienced embolic or bleeding complications. Conclusion: AF was uncommon during zanubrutinib treatment, even in the higher-risk subgroup. Historical comparisons remain limited, and exploratory score findings require confirmation with longer follow-up. Trial Registration: The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

title: Age-adjusted baseline D-dimer predicts thrombotic events during readmission in anticoagulated patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation
authors: Xiaosu Wang; Li Zhang; Dan Zhang; Jingdan Yu; Zheng Dai; Qichao Li; Xinsheng Yan
abstract: Abstract Background Patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) remain at substantial risk of thrombotic and bleeding events despite oral anticoagulation, and readmission is a common and costly consequence. D-dimer reflects persistent coagulation and fibrinolysis activation and has been associated with adverse outcomes in atrial fibrillation, but whether a single baseline measurement can predict events during readmission remains unclear. Methods We retrospectively studied 1,108 anticoagulated patients with NVAF who had multiple hospitalisations at our institution between 2018 and 2022. Patients were stratified by baseline D-dimer according to an age-adjusted cut-off. The primary endpoint was a composite of thrombotic events, major bleeding and death during readmission, adjudicated by a hierarchical first-event rule. Multivariable Cox regression was performed in the 899 patients with complete CHA₂DS₂-VASc and HAS-BLED scores. Sensitivity analyses included propensity score matching (230 pairs) and a competing-risk model and a 30-day landmark analysis. The incremental value of the age-adjusted D-dimer cut-off beyond CHA₂DS₂-VASc was assessed by the C-statistic. Results The abnormal-D-dimer group had a higher incidence of the composite endpoint (24.0% vs 9.6%, P < 0.001) and of thrombotic events (19.7% vs 8.2%, P < 0.001). Abnormal D-dimer independently predicted the composite endpoint (adjusted HR 1.64, 95% CI 1.09–2.47) and thrombotic events (adjusted HR 2.02, 95% CI 1.30–3.15), but not major bleeding (HR 1.46, 95% CI 0.44–4.90) or death during readmission (HR 1.73, 95% CI 0.54–5.52). Sensitivity analyses were consistent for the composite and thrombotic endpoints, whereas bleeding and death events were too few for reliable estimates. Adding D-dimer to CHA₂DS₂-VASc improved discrimination (ΔC = 0.034, 95% CI 0.006–0.076) and reclassification (24-month NRI = 43.8%; IDI = 0.025). Conclusions In anticoagulated patients with NVAF, a baseline D-dimer above the age-adjusted cut-off independently predicts thrombotic events during subsequent readmission and provides incremental predictive information beyond CHA₂DS₂-VASc.

title: Acute Pulmonary Oedema and Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure During a Probable Autonomic Dysreflexic Episode in Chronic Cervical Spinal Cord Injury: A Case Report
authors: Ameen Ghannoum; Amy-Claire Young; Ranganatha Rao
abstract: Autonomic dysreflexia is a life-threatening complication affecting individuals with spinal cord injuries at or above the sixth thoracic level.While episodic hypertension is its clinical hallmark, serious cardiovascular and respiratory complications may occur.We report the case of a 67-year-old male with long-standing C5-C6 tetraplegia and established autonomic dysreflexia who was admitted with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP).At approximately 01:00 on hospital day 4, after receiving approximately 3 L of maintenance intravenous fluid for poor oral intake over the preceding 72 hours, he developed sudden severe breathlessness and loss of consciousness despite a previously improving oxygen requirement.Oxygen saturation fell to 77% despite oxygen therapy, while systolic blood pressure rose from a baseline of approximately 125-130 mmHg to 167 mmHg.Physical examination revealed bilateral crackles and reduced air entry.Arterial blood gas analysis showed profound hypercapnic acidaemia (pH 7.009; partial pressure of carbon dioxide 18.5 kPa).A chest radiograph showed rapidly progressive bilateral airspace opacities consistent with pulmonary oedema.His blood pressure returned towards baseline, and following highconcentration oxygen and intravenous furosemide, his oxygen requirement subsequently decreased.Computed tomography pulmonary angiography excluded pulmonary embolism, and echocardiography showed low-normal left ventricular systolic function without a major structural or valvular abnormality.The sudden respiratory deterioration, clinically significant rise in blood pressure from baseline, rapid radiographic evolution, and subsequent improvement supported acute pulmonary oedema occurring during a probable autonomic dysreflexic episode.No discrete precipitating stimulus was confirmed, although concurrent pneumonia was considered the most likely trigger for autonomic dysreflexia.Recent intravenous fluid administration and underlying cardiac vulnerability may have lowered the threshold for pulmonary oedema.This case highlights the importance of recognising a clinically meaningful rise from baseline blood pressure when a patient with high spinal cord injury develops sudden respiratory deterioration.

title: Task Force 5: Clinical Considerations for Myocarditis and Selected Cardiovascular Conditions, Including Valvular Heart Disease
authors: James Sawalla Guseh; LARRY A. ALLEN; SILVIA CASTELLETTI; Aaron Leigh Baggish; BENJAMIN D. LEVINE; Jonathan H. Kim; Matthias Wilhelm; MATTHEW W. MARTINEZ
abstract: Athletes with myocarditis, pericarditis, valvular heart disease, and other acquired cardiovascular conditions require careful evaluation when considering competitive sports participation. This document outlines key clinical considerations, risk factors, and expert consensus, serving as the rationale for Section V of the recent AHA/ACC Scientific Statement: Clinical Considerations for Competitive Sports Participation for Athletes with Cardiovascular Abnormalities. Disease-specific risk stratification and shared decision-making are essential in determining return-to-play eligibility. This Task Force document addresses myocarditis, pericarditis, the cardiovascular impact of respiratory viral infections, incidental myocardial fibrosis, Kawasaki disease, infiltrative cardiomyopathies, and valvular heart disease.

title: The role of PDCD4 in the peripheral T cell immune microenvironment of non-valvular atrial fibrillation
authors: Jiao Wang; Meijuan Zheng; Jing Zhou; 杨玉春; Huyati Mu
abstract: Abstract The immune and inflammatory mechanisms underlying non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) are not fully understood. Programmed cell death 4 (PDCD4) is a transcriptional and translational inhibitor associated with pro-inflammatory activity and fibrotic remodeling in cardiac tissues. This study assessed the regulatory role of PDCD4 in T lymphocyte responses in the peripheral blood of NVAF patients. We utilized an open single-cell transcriptome dataset containing peripheral blood mononuclear cell samples from patients with drug-related paroxysmal atrial fibrillation during the medication period and the withdrawal period, combined with bioinformatics analysis, to preliminarily explore the role of PDCD4 in inflammatory response, cytokine secretion, and immune regulation. We collected peripheral blood from patients and matched non-AF controls and performed flow cytometry to (1) quantify PDCD4 expression in T-cell subsets, (2) determine the percentage of cytokine-positive PDCD4 + and PDCD4– T cells, and (3) quantify the expression of surface co-stimulatory and co-inhibitory receptors after in vitro stimulation with or without PDCD4-IN-1. T cell vitality was measured using the CCK-8 assay, and cytokine secretion was assessed by ELISA. Single-cell transcriptome analysis revealed that PDCD4 was highly expressed in activated CD8 + T cells from AF group. PDCD4-expressing cells exhibited strong enrichment for T-cell receptor signaling, cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction, and complement activation. Flow cytometry showed that PDCD4 expression was significantly higher in CD4 + T cells, CD8 + T cells, and Treg cells in the NVAF group (all P < 0.001). The secretion of IL-4, IL-17 A, IL-10, and IFN-γ was significantly higher in PDCD4 + T cells than in PDCD4 − T cells ( P < 0.05). PDCD4 inhibition reduced the percentage of CD8 + CD137 + T cells ( P < 0.001), T cell vitality ( P < 0.01), and the secretion of the proinflammatory cytokines IFN-γ and TNF-α ( P < 0.001). PDCD4 affects the immune microenvironment in NVAF by promoting peripheral T cell activation, and inflammatory cytokine secretion.

title: Task Force 10: Clinical Considerations for the Care of Masters Athletes with Underlying Cardiovascular Disease
authors: Elizabeth H. Dineen; Mats B rjesson; Eugene H. Chung; Thijs M H Eijsvogels; Aaron Leigh Baggish; BENJAMIN D. LEVINE; Paul D. Thompson; Jonathan H. Kim
abstract: Masters athletes are individuals ≥35 yr of age who place a high premium on exercise training and competition. This document details important cardiovascular conditions, risk factors, and data-driven discussion, which serve as the rationale for Section X from the 2025 AHA/ACC Scientific Statement: Clinical Considerations for Competitive Sports Participation for Athletes Cardiovascular Abnormalities. Disease-specific risk stratification and shared decision-making are the cornerstones for Masters athletes when considering competitive sports participation. Coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, incidental myocardial fibrosis, aortic enlargement and aneurysms, and valvular heart disease are included in this Task Force document.

title: Subclinical Left Ventricular Myocardial Impairment and the Threshold Effect of Intact Parathyroid Hormone in Maintenance Hemodialysis Patients with Secondary Hyperparathyroidism: A Two-Dimensional Speckle-Tracking Echocardiographic Study
authors: Fan Zhang; Yumei Duan; Qinyue Yang; Linying Shu; Jing Bai; Hongguang Sun
abstract: Abstract Background To investigate the value of two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (2D-STE)-derived global longitudinal strain (GLS), 17-segment strain and peak strain dispersion (PSD) for detecting left ventricular myocardial impairment in maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) patients with secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT), and to define the cutoff of intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH) that signals myocardial impairment. Methods A total of 88 consecutive maintenance hemodialysis patients fulfilling the diagnostic criteria of SHPT (December 2023–December 2025) were retrospectively enrolled and divided by iPTH into a low-PTH group (n = 36) and a high-PTH group (n = 52); 43 healthy volunteers served as controls. All underwent 2D-STE. Myocardial impairment was defined as an absolute GLS < 16%. Logistic regression and ROC analysis assessed the predictive performance and optimal cutoff of iPTH. Patients were followed up until July 2026, and Cox regression was used exploratorily for cardiovascular events. Results GLS decreased stepwise across the three groups (17.6%, 16.5% and 12.2%; P < 0.001). Although EF was normal in all 88 dialysis patients, GLS was already < 16% in 71.6%. Segmental strain showed a basal-predominant, relatively apically preserved pattern (high- vs. low-PTH: basal 11.32% vs. 15.39%, apical 14.51% vs. 18.78%, both P < 0.001), and PSD was higher in the high- than in the low-PTH group (75.60 vs. 55.00 ms, P < 0.001). iPTH was an independent determinant of GLS (β = −0.0044, P < 0.001); each 100 pg/mL increase conferred a 3.8-fold higher odds of myocardial impairment (adjusted OR 4.531, 95% CI 1.978–10.380, P < 0.001), with an optimal cutoff of 190.8 pg/mL (AUC 0.859, sensitivity 82.5%, specificity 92.0%). In exploratory Cox regression (median follow-up 22.0 months), only age remained an independent predictor. Conclusions Patients with MHD complicated by SHPT have subclinical myocardial impairment preceding the decline in EF, characterized by reduced global GLS, a basal-predominant segmental pattern with relative apical preservation, and impaired mechanical synchrony. The iPTH–impairment association is threshold-like, and approximately 190.8 pg/mL may serve as a warning cutoff. Combining GLS with 17-segment strain and PSD may allow earlier detection of myocardial impairment.

title: Intravenous loop diuretic timing and renal outcomes after cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury
authors: Jinjing Wu; Tiantian Sun; Peirong Lin; Sheng Wang
abstract: Intravenous loop diuretics are frequently used for fluid removal after cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI), but the implications of initiation timing remain uncertain. We used MIMIC-IV v3.1 in a retrospective observational study informed by target-trial principles. Adults with AKI after cardiac surgery were assigned time zero at the first qualifying KDIGO AKI timestamp and classified by qualifying intravenous loop diuretic exposure timing within 72 h: Early (active at T0 or initiated within 0–24 h), Late (> 24–72 h), or None. The primary outcome was Day-7 renal recovery; secondary outcomes included Day-30 recovery, persistent AKI, acute kidney disease, and MAKE30. Stabilized inverse-probability-of-treatment weights from a multinomial propensity-score model were truncated at the 99.5th percentile. Among 6,289 patients, Early versus None showed no clear difference in Day-7 renal recovery (74.8 vs. 74.0%; risk difference, 0.77% points; 95% CI, −3.30 to 4.94). This finding remained compatible with the null in the propensity-score-refit bootstrap (95% CI, −3.59 to 5.18) and a 72-hour survivor-restricted analysis (risk difference, 0.27% points; 95% CI, −3.76 to 4.36). Secondary Early-versus-Late contrasts showed differences for some outcomes but were exploratory and statistically fragile given the small Late group, and they do not override the primary comparison, which showed no clear benefit or harm.

title: Inverse association between serum osteocalcin and pericardial adipose tissue in Koreans: cross-sectional study
authors: Myeongjin Shin; Beom-Hee Choi; Nam‐Seok Joo
abstract: Background: Osteocalcin (OC), a bone matrix protein of osteoblastic origin, is thought to play a role in systemic metabolic function. However, the relationship between serum OC levels and pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) volume remains unclear. Methods: Using a cross-sectional design, 438 participants (88 females, 350 males) who underwent cardiac CT imaging were enrolled. Simple and partial correlation analyses were performed. OC levels were divided into tertile groups to assess their relationship with PAT, adjusting for age, sex, smoking, hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Linear and logistic regression models were also applied. Results: The mean participant age was 55.7 years. The average serum OC level was 15.9 ng/mL, and the mean PAT volume was 127.6 cm3. OC level and PAT volume showed an inverse correlation that was significant in both unadjusted (r=-0.158, P=0.001) and covariate-adjusted (r=-0.106, P=0.032) analyses. Inter-tertile PAT differences remained significant after stratification (P<0.05). In multivariate regression analysis, the inverse association remained statistically significant after adjustment for age, sex and smoking (P=0.019), but not after additional adjustment for body mass index (P=0.656). After adjustment, relative to the highest OC tertile, the odds ratios for being classified into the highest PAT tertile were 2.73 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.43-5.21) for the lowest and 2.99 (95% CI, 1.59-5.66) for the middle OC tertile. Conclusion: Serum OC level was inversely associated with PAT volume; however, this association was attenuated after adjusting for adiposity-related variables, suggesting that shared metabolic or body composition factors may partly account for the observed relationship.
